  d_p(G)=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V(G)}\frac{e(G[S])}{|S|^p}. \] We determine the sharp asymptotic upper bound for $λ(G)$ in terms of $d_p(G)$ and $n$. More precisely, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with at least one edge satisfies \[ λ(G)\le \begin{cases} \left(\left(\max_{t\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}\dfrac{t}{(t+1)^p}\right)^{-1}+o(1)\right)d_p(G)\sqrt n,&1<p<3/2,\\[0.4em] \left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{4}+o(1)\right)d_p(G)\sqrt{n\log n},&p=3/2,\\[0.4em] (\mathfrak C_p+o(1))d_p(G)n^{p-1},&3/2<p<2, \end{cases} \] and each constant here is best possible. Here $\mathfrak C_p$ is characterized by an exact variational problem over finite kernels. We apply a sparse graphon operator estimate to convert hereditary $p$-density bounds into sharp spectral bounds, and this estimate also explains the transition at the critical exponent $p=3/2$. For the endpoint $p=2$, Wilf's theorem gives the exact finite-$n$ bound $λ(G)\le 2d_2(G)n$, with equality for $K_n$. Thus Guiduli's power-law problem is resolved in its sharp asymptotic form for every $1<p\leq2$, including exact leading constants.

papers.title: A Kernel-Clean Lean Mechanization of Classical Lottery in Action and the Wakker--Debreu--Koopmans Representation Layer
papers.summary: We present a Lean 4/Mathlib formalization of the additive representation theory behind Classical Lottery in Action and the Wakker-Debreu-Koopmans (WDK) layer it relies on. Our central result is a machine-checked proof that the cross-pair Thomsen / double-cancellation (hexagon) condition is irreducible from the ordinal axioms of additive conjoint measurement (weak order, restricted solvability, Archimedean condition, and tradeoff consistency). We exhibit an explicit verified counter-model (additiveRealBoolPref) satisfying all ordinal axioms yet failing the cross-pair condition, with every strict standard sequence being an arithmetic progression and hence non-dense. Around this boundary we mechanize the full derivable construction: continuous Debreu/Eilenberg utility from separability, standard-sequence grids, bisection methods from connectedness, and global additive gluing. All public theorems are sorry-free conditional wrappers over this single irreducible structural input. The development is kernel-clean, depending only on standard Lean foundations (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The companion file ClassicalLotteryInAction.lean formalizes local classical-lottery constructions, average-utility results, matching-frequency lemmas, and ambiguity-attitude statements used by the Management Science paper. This draws a precise, machine-certified line between what additive conjoint measurement can prove and what it must assume.

papers.title: One-dimensional first return maps for the two-dimensional border-collision normal form with a zero determinant
papers.summary: The two-dimensional border-collision normal form is a four-parameter family of continuous, piecewise-linear maps. When this form has a zero determinant, all of its nonlinear dynamics are captured a one-dimensional first return map. The first return map is discontinuous and piecewise-linear, where each piece of the map corresponds to a constant return time. We show that when the normal form has a repelling focus fixed point, the configuration of the first return map is dictated by a rational rotation number whereby the set of return times and ordering of the pieces of the map are given by the denominators of the left and right sequences of Farey parents of this number. The result is proved by characterising polygons formed from preimages of the switching manifold, and employing an inductive argument on the Farey web. Several surfaces in parameter space where the configuration changes are bifurcations from chaotic to quasiperiodic or mode-locked dynamics.

papers.title: Polynomial Corners Over finite Fields
papers.summary:
Recently there has been some progress in understanding the density of a subset of $[N]^2$ that avoids polynomial patterns. Kravitz, Kuca, and Leng showed that if $P\in\mathbb{Z}[z]$ satisfies certain conditions, then any set $A\subseteq[N]^2$ does not contain $(x,y),(x+P(z),y),(x,y+P(z))$, we must have
  \[
  |A|\ll_P\frac{N^2}{(\log\log\log N)^c}
  \]
  for some small constant $c$.
  In this article, we show a similar result in $(\mathbb{F}_p)^2$ where we get a better bound on the density of a set $A\subseteq (\mathbb{F}_p)^2$ not containing $(x,y),(x+P(z),y),(x,y+P(z))$ with some conditions on $P\in \mathbb{F}_p[z]$.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10193v1.title: 最小周期的分解に対するモジュラー構造定理と P_η(4,n) ≤ 4n を満たす配置の周期性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10193v1.summary: Nivat 予想は、矩形パターン複雑度が P_η(k,n) ≤ kn を満たす2次元配置 η が必ず周期的であるという予想である。本論文では、Kari-Szabados の代数的枠組みと周期的分解および片側非拡大方向に関する最新の知見を活用し、Cyr-Kra による k ≤ 3 の結果を P_η(4,n) ≤ 4n の場合へと拡張した。その鍵として、低凸パターン複雑度を持つ非周期的配置に対し、その成分が特定の法 p において複数の半平面上で同時に完全周期的となるような ℤ-最小周期的分解の存在を示す構造定理を導出している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10193v1.appendix: 本論文は興味ある分野のうち symbolic dynamics および combinatorics on words に強く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10168v1.title: 三角行列群における generalized torsion
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10168v1.summary: 本論文では、ある元の共役の有限積が単位元となる「generalized torsion」という概念について、可換環上の上三角行列群における特徴付けを行っている。また、基礎となる環の単位元群の捩れや指数の性質を用いて、これらの行列群がいつ generalized identity を満たすかを決定した。応用として、特定の長さの generalized identity を満たす有限生成無限可解群の新たな族を構築し、Sherman の問いに対する反例を示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10168v1.appendix: 本論文は、無限可解群の構造や generalized identity を扱っており、「structure of large countable infinite group」の分野に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10155v1.title: 分散型ビリヤードへの転送作用素の適用における最近の進展
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10155v1.summary: 本論文は、ハイパーボリック・ビリヤードの統計的性質を研究するための転送作用素の活用に関するレビュー論文である。主な焦点は、平衡状態、逐次ビリヤード、およびビリヤード流における相関の減衰に当てられている。既存の文献を概観するだけでなく、主要なアイデアの具体化やそれらの相互関係の解明、さらには議論されている問題が位置する広範な背景についても解説している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10155v1.appendix: 本論文で扱われるハイパーボリック・ビリヤードや転送作用素の解析は、興味ある分野に含まれる symbolic dynamics と密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10102v1.title: 多角形におけるビリヤードの周期軌道の存在
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10102v1.summary: 任意の有限多角形内のビリヤード流が少なくとも一つの周期軌道を持つことを証明している。この証明は背理法を用いており、Galperin、Krüger、Troubetzkoyによるビリヤード流の力学に関する基礎的な結果、単位接束上の自然なリーマン計量の1パラメータスケーリングの幾何学、およびスケーリングされた計量のスケルトン（またはカットローカス）のトポロジーに基づいている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10102v1.appendix: 本論文は、軌跡の符号化による解析という観点から、興味ある分野のsymbolic dynamicsと関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10059v1.title: Worsening Trickを用いた書換規則の有限状態変換器へのコンパイル
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10059v1.summary: 本論文は、自然言語処理等の分野で音韻・形態論的書換規則（A → B / L _ R）を有限状態変換器（FST）へコンパイルするための新しい手法を提案している。従来のKaplan and KayやKarttunenらによる手法は、補助記号を用いた複雑な合成を必要としていたが、本手法は「worsening trick」に基づき、まず全ての合法な候補を生成し、同一入力に対して他より劣る（worse）候補をフィルタリングするという簡潔な構成をとる。この手法はPyFomaに実装されており、多重文脈、重み付き書換、並列書換など多様な様態をサポートする。検証の結果、従来のfoma等の実装と同一の変換器を生成しつつ、より拡張性に優れた短い定式化が可能であることが示された。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10059v1.appendix: 本論文は興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」および「formal languages」に直接関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10035v1.title: Dyckパスの高さと市松模様のラベル付け
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10035v1.summary: Dyckパスとノードに対する特定の白黒のラベル付けから導かれる「白の高さ（white-height）」という概念について考察している。母関数を用いた解析手法により、長さ2nのDyckパスにおける平均的な白の高さが、2種類の異なるモデルにおいて1/2√(πn)に漸近することを証明した。組み合わせ論における標準的な手法を学ぶための教材としても適した、魅力的な結果が提示されている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10035v1.appendix: 本論文は、提示された興味ある分野のうち「combinatorics on words」および「formal languages」に密接に関連しています。平均的な高さの漸近的振る舞いが 1/2√(πn) となることを導出しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10033v1.title: アンチ・ヘルダー・ポテンシャルに対するリアプノフ指数の一様正値性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10033v1.summary: 双曲力学系によって生成される、アンチα-Hölder連続な動的定義ポテンシャルを持つシュレーディンガー作用素を考察する。関連する射影化コサイクル下でのe₁の軌道に関連する関数について、アンチ・リプシッツ評価を証明した。この評価を有限型サブシフトや、d≧1のトーラス上で拡大方向を1つ持つ写像に適用した。その結果、結合定数が十分に大きい場合に、リアプノフ指数が一様正値となることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10033v1.appendix: この論文は、有限型サブシフトを扱っていることから興味ある分野の「symbolic dynamics」に関連しています。また、力学系に基づいたポテンシャルや写像を扱っており「complex dynamics」などの力学系理論全般にも関連する内容です。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10007v1.title: 有理写像の自守測度、リアプノフ指数、および不安定性について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10007v1.summary: Julia集合内に非総和的な臨界点を持つ有理写像の不安定性の障害を構成するため、複素固有値を持つ「自守測度」を導入した。この測度は、Radon-Nikodym微分が複素値かつ一般化された自守因子 j₍ₛ,ₜ₎(R) = |R'|ˢ (|R'|/R')ᵗ に比例することを許容することで、従来の準不変測度や共形測度を拡張したものである。本論文では、特定の自守測度（特にユニモジュラ測度）の存在が、対応する写像の不安定性を意味することを示した。具体的には、(-1, 1)-ユニモジュラ測度を持つ弱散逸的な有理写像が q ≥ 1 に対して q-不安定であることを証明し、従来の不安定性基準を一般化した。また、有界再帰性や Milnor-Thurston の kneading theory を通じて、これらの測度の存在を保証するエルゴード的および組合せ論的条件を確立している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10007v1.appendix: 興味ある分野のうち「complex dynamics」に直接関連しています。また、Milnor-Thurston の kneading theory との関連性など、力学系の組合せ論的な側面にも触れられています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09822v1.title: 形式言語タスクの学習可能性における因果的評価
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09822v1.summary: 言語モデルが特定のタスクを学習するために必要なデータ量を、自然言語の設定で正確に測定することは、タスク間の交絡や境界の曖昧さから困難である。本論文では、確率的有限オートマトンから誘導される形式言語を制御されたテストベッドとして用い、従来の相関ベースの評価手法が本質的に欠陥を抱えていることを示した。因果分析を可能にするため、コーパス内の特定の性質の出現頻度を制御できる代数的対象「binning semiring」を導入し、因果グラフィカルモデルと言語モデルの学習可能性を評価するための分解されたKullback-Leibler(KL)情報量指標を定式化した。実験の結果、因果的介入のない評価は交絡因子によって誤った結論を導くことが明らかになり、自然言語設定における相関分析の落とし穴について警鐘を鳴らしている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09822v1.appendix: 本論文は、提示された興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」および「formal languages」に深く関連しています。確率的有限オートマトンを用いた形式言語の学習プロセスを、代数的な半環構造（binning semiring）を用いて解析するアプローチをとっています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09795v1.title: 層比モンテカルロ法によるデデキント数の有限n推定
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09795v1.summary: デデキント数は単調ブール関数の総数、あるいはブール束の下方集合（downsets）の数として定義される。本論文では、この数え上げをランク付けされたイデアル束のホイットニー数に関する層比再構成問題として定式化し、可逆な固定層マルコフ連鎖を用いたモンテカルロ法によってデデキント数 M(n) を推定する手法を提案している。M(8) および M(9) でのバックテストを通じて誤差の較正を行い、M(10) の値を (8.9360 ± 0.0010) × 10⁷⁸ と推定した。また、従来は経験的に単峰的（unimodal）とされていたイデアル束のホイットニー数配列について、高精度な推定に基づき、中央ランク付近に「二つの肩」状の構造が存在することを明らかにした。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09795v1.appendix: 本論文は「combinatorics on words」に関連する組合せ論的数え上げ、および巨大な数値を統計的に扱う手法（validated numerics との緩やかな関連）を扱っています。デデキント数の計算は計算困難な問題として知られており、本研究はマルコフ連鎖モンテカルロ法を用いて M(10) という極めて巨大な値に対して高精度な近似を与えています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09743v1.title: 自己相似測度の非線形像のフーリエ変換：定性的側面
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09743v1.summary: 本論文の目的は、十分な非線形性を持つ実解析的写像 f: ℝᵏ → ℝᵈ による ℝᵏ 上の自己相似測度 μ の像について、多項式的フーリエ減衰を確立することである。例えば、f が解析的でそのグラフが ℝᵏ⁺ᵈ のアフィン超平面に含まれず、μ が ℝᵏ のアフィン超平面に台を持たない場合、像測度は多項式的フーリエ減衰を示す。証明の鍵となるのは、自己相似測度に対する一様なロヤシェヴィッチ型の不等式の確立、および非常に小さな例外集合の外側における μ のフーリエ変換の減衰を利用することである。応用として、線形IFSと解析的に共役な複素解析的IFSから得られる、複素平面 ℂ 上の自己共形測度に対する多項式的フーリエ減衰を証明している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09743v1.appendix: 本論文は「complex dynamics」に関連しています。自己共形測度や複素解析的な反復関数系（IFS）の解析は、複素力学系の性質を理解する上で重要なトピックです。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09702v1.title: プロ有限剛性、Grothendieck対、およびいくつかの3次元オービフォールド群の2次ホモロジーについて
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09702v1.summary: 3次元多様体群のプロ有限剛性の研究において、2次ホモロジー群は中心的な重要性を持つ。本論文では、双曲的有理ホモロジー3次元球面の基本群の有限拡大として現れるオービフォールド群に対して、H₂を計算するための効果的な手法を開発した。この手法をWeeks多様体に関連するすべての余コンパクト格子に適用し、それらが絶対プロ有限剛性を持つことを証明した。また、BridsonとReidの問いに答える形で、特定の四元数環の極大語に関連する群の2次ホモロジーがℤ/2ℤであることを示した。さらに、この結果を利用して、ある格子の直積群におけるGrothendieck対の存在を示し、最後にFibonacci多様体Mₙの基本群の有限拡大についてもH₂の計算を行った。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09702v1.appendix: 本論文は、プロ有限剛性や群のホモロジー的性質を扱っており、巨大な可算無限群の構造 (structure of large countable infinite group) に関する分野と関連がある。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09696v1.title: 等エネルギー退化は一般に蛇行不変トーラスを生成する
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09696v1.summary: 2自由度の等エネルギー退化可積分ハミルトン系において、一般的なハミルトニアンに対するカスプ一般的な摂動が、グラフ構造を持たない埋め込まれたラグランジュ・トーラスである「蛇行不変トーラス（meandering invariant tori）」を生成することを明らかにしている。さらに、摂動の指数的に密な部分集合内では、2次から無限次までの高次の蛇行トーラスが存在し、特に無限次の蛇行は無限の入れ子構造を形成することを示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09696v1.appendix: ハミルトン力学系およびシンプレクティック幾何学における不変集合のトポロジーに関する研究です。提示された「興味ある分野」の中では、不変集合が持つ無限の入れ子構造という点で complex dynamics や symbolic dynamics との関連性が考えられます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09674v1.title: (自動)形式化は容易であるはずだ：厳密な証明を詳細に記述するためのTrellisプロセスセマンティクス
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09674v1.summary: LLMエージェントと決定論的に制約されたワークフローを組み合わせ、Leanを用いた数学的証明の自動形式化を段階的に進展させるシステム「Trellis」を提案する。本手法は、厳密な証明とはいかなる部分も詳細に具体化（精緻化）できるものであるという数学的な概念に基づいており、自然言語の証明を反復的に洗練させることで形式化を実現する。特化型の訓練ではなく、プロセスセマンティクスによる厳密なワークフローの強制によって、汎用的なエージェントでも低コストで信頼性の高い形式化を可能にしている。実証として、ラムゼー理論における最新の研究成果をLeanで形式化した例を挙げている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09674v1.appendix: 本論文はラムゼー理論の最新の成果の形式化に言及しており、計算機科学的な観点から formal languages (形式言語) や証明の厳密性に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09673v1.title: 有限フォン・ノイマン環における一様回帰的部分環 (Uniformly recurrent subalgebras)
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09673v1.summary: 可算離散群 Γ の有限フォン・ノイマン環 M へのトレース保存作用に対し、一様回帰的部分群 (URS) の作用素環論的な対応概念として一様回帰的部分環 (URA) を導入した。Effros-Maréchal 空間 Sub(M) がコンパクトであるための必要十分条件が M が拡散的な直和成分を持たないことであることを示し、これを利用して任意の極小ポーランド空間に同相なエキゾチックな URA を構成した。また、アメナブルな係数を持つ接合積 M ⋊ Γ において、Γ が C*-単純であることと、M を含む接合積の唯一のアメナブルな URA が {M} であることが同値であることを証明した。さらに、Sub(M) のコンパクト性の欠如を補うため、トレース延長状態の弱*コンパクト空間上のベールのカテゴリ法を用いた一般化状態空間の枠組みを開発し、古典的な URS の枠組みを特殊なケースとして包含することを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09673v1.appendix: 本論文は、可算離散群の作用や接合積の構造、C*-単純性の判定条件を扱っており、興味ある分野である「structure of large countable infinite group」に深く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09415v1.title: 比較可能グラフの和集合の彩色数について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09415v1.summary: 1980年代にGyárfásによって提示された2つの完全グラフの和集合に関する古い問題を強い意味で解決した。本論文では、任意の正の整数dおよびkに対して、クリーク数がkかつ彩色数がkᵈであり、かつd個の比較可能グラフの和集合として表されるグラフGが存在することを証明した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09415v1.appendix: 本論文はグラフ理論および離散数学における古典的な問題を扱っており、提示された分野の中では「combinatorics on words」と広い意味での組合せ論（combinatorics）という文脈で関連性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09321v2.title: Ballantine, Beck, Merca, および Sagan による Elementary Symmetric Partitions に関する予想 19 の証明
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09321v2.summary: Ballantineらによって提唱された、整数分割（integer partitions）上の写像 preₖ の像とOEIS（オンライン整数列大辞典）の特定の数列を関連付ける4つの恒等式からなる「Conjecture 19」を検証した論文である。本論文では、(i) および (iii) を無条件で証明し、(iv) については別の予想（Conjecture 1）の単射性を用いることで証明し、かつその単射性が (iv) と同値であることを示した。(ii) に関しては分割論的な側面を無条件で証明した上で、残る部分をハフマン符号化に関連する Dean Hickerson の予想へと帰着させた。また、既報の (iii) における符号の誤りを修正し、正しい恒等式が χ(ImP₃(n)) = A213213(n) - 1 であることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09321v2.appendix: 本論文は整数分割の組合せ論的性質を扱っており、提示された「興味ある分野」に直接合致する項目は含まれていませんが、数え上げ組合せ論や離散数学の範疇に属する研究です。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09224v1.title: 右群、左準群、および右ヒープ
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09224v1.summary: 本論文では、右群（任意の a, b ∈ S に対して a ・ x = b が一意の解 x ∈ S を持つ半群）を基礎としたヒープ（heap）の理論を発展させ、右ヒープ（right heap）の概念を定義している。さらに、右群の非結合的な対応物である左準群（left quasigroup）から理論の一部を構築することも可能であることを示している。この研究の動機は、ヤン・バクスター方程式（Yang-Baxter equation）の左非退化集合論的解の調査にあり、T. Brzeziński が導入した skew left truss の類似構造の導出に至っている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09224v1.appendix: 本論文は代数的構造（群やヒープの一般化）を扱っており、ヤン・バクスター方程式の解の構造に関連しています。直接的には[興味ある分野]のリストに含まれる特定の分野を主題としたものではありませんが、群の構造（structure of large countable infinite group）に関連する代数学的な基盤を提供しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09207v1.title: 多数の共存するアトラクタ：ほとんど保存的なHénon写像のケーススタディ
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09207v1.summary: 2次元の力学系において、有界な領域内に多数の周期アトラクタが共存することがあり、これらは散逸が極めて小さい「ほとんど保存的（almost-conservative）」な系で見つかりやすくなる。本研究では、微小な散逸を持つHénon写像を事例として取り上げ、50個の吸引的周期軌道（合計4259個の周期点）が存在するパラメータ設定を詳しく解析した。これらの軌道は、2つの低周期軌道を除き、主に3つのファミリーに分類・整理できることを明らかにしている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09207v1.appendix: 本論文は力学系の数値的な振る舞いを扱っており、指定された興味ある分野の中では complex dynamics や validated numerics に関連する内容を含んでいます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09158v1.title: q元ハミング球の共通部分のサイズ
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09158v1.summary: DNAデータストレージシステムの進展を背景に、異なる半径を持つs個のq元ハミング球の共通部分のサイズ（基数）を求める厳密な公式を提案している。一般に、中心点間の距離だけでは共通部分のサイズを確定させるには不十分であるが、本論文の公式を用いることで、サイズを決定するための中心点の詳細な構造的特性を明らかにできる。また、nが十分に大きい場合についても解析し、特にs=3において中心点間の最小距離が予えられた際に共通部分が最大となる必要十分条件（q≥2かつq≠6の場合）を導出している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09158v1.appendix: 本論文は、ハミング空間における組合せ論的な解析を扱っており、興味ある分野のうち「combinatorics on words」に関連する側面を持っています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09045v1.title: 有限集合上の関数の可換環上の低次多項式への埋め込み
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09045v1.summary: 有限集合 X 上の関数 f: Xᵏ → X を、単射 j: X → R を用いて可換環 R 上の次数 d 以下の多項式 g で表現する（j ∘ f = g ∘ jᵏ）「埋め込み」について研究した論文である。これは、遷移構造を保持しながらアルファベットを拡張する k 近傍セル・オートマトンの遷移関数に対応する。本論文では Lean 4 を用いて、すべての 1 変数関数は次数 1 で埋め込み可能であること、2 変数クロネッカーのデルタは次数 4 で埋め込み可能であること、そして任意の次数 d に対して埋め込み不可能な 2 変数関数が存在することを証明した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09045v1.appendix: 本論文はセル・オートマトンの遷移関数を多項式表現として扱っているため、興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」に関連しています。また、結果が定理証明支援系 Lean 4 と Mathlib を用いて形式的に検証されている点が特徴です。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09031v1.title: コンパクト複素曲面上のランダム斜積における最大エントロピー測度
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09031v1.summary: コンパクト複素曲面 X 上の自己同型群 Aut(X) におけるボレル確率測度 μ に付随する斜積が、対数可積分条件およびその台が非基本的部分群を生成するという条件の下で、一意な最大ファイバーエントロピー不変測度を持つことを証明した。この測度は Cantat と Dujardin が構築したランダム極限電流を用いて標準的に記述され、そのファイバーエントロピーはコホモロジー上のランダム作用に付随する Furstenberg 指数に等しい。また、指数モーメントの仮定の下で、この測度が混合的であることを示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09031v1.appendix: 本論文は、複素動力学 (complex dynamics) の分野と強く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08991v1.title: 最小非自明回転ハミング距離が2であるバイナリネックレス
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08991v1.summary: 本論文では、代表元に依存しない最小非自明回転ハミング距離 minDist(w) が2となるバイナリネックレス [w] の分類と数え上げを行っている。これは周期的なケースの次に位置する最初の正の層である。距離2を与える非ゼロのシフト集合に基づき、優先順位を用いてハーフターン(HT)、シングルペア(SP)、部分群パターン(SUB)の各クラスに分類し、マルチペア(MP)クラスが空であることを示した。各クラスの数に対する閉じた式や、総数 |D₂(n)| を求めるためのメビウスの反転公式とトーシェント関数を用いた約数和公式を導出している。また、SUBケースと境界ケースを含む「部分群型」の分岐を、商背景正規形を用いて記述した。特に奇素数長 p の場合、距離2のネックレスはすべて素数サイクル上の算術区間と回転同値であり、その総数は (p² - 4p + 7)/2 となる。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08991v1.appendix: この論文は、提示された興味ある分野の中で「symbolic dynamics」および「combinatorics on words」に密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08983v1.title: 低階数分離可能場セル・オートマトンにおけるダイナミクス
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08983v1.summary: 本論文では、局所的な近傍の数え上げをランク1の行・列分離場に置き換えた「分離可能場セル・オートマトン（SFCA）」を提案し、その集団力学を調査した。生存と誕生を制御する閾値インターバルの体系的なスキャンにより、絶滅、不動点、周期軌道、長期的過渡状態の4つのクラスが特定された。特に、生存インターバルと誕生インターバルの相対的な幾何配置が力学系を決定し、特定の境界領域において長期的過渡状態が安定して現れることが判明した。損傷波及解析の結果、この過渡状態は2つの周期アトラクタ・ファミリー間の選択の遅延を反映しており、圧縮された分離場結合下でも非自明な集団組織化が可能であることが示唆された。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08983v1.appendix: 本論文は、complex dynamicsの分野に関連しています。特に、セル・オートマトンにおけるパターンの形成や、アトラクタ間の遷移といった複雑な動的挙動の解析が含まれています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08901v1.title: 行列式が0である2次元境界衝突標準形の1次元第1帰還写像
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08901v1.summary: 2次元境界衝突標準形は、4つのパラメータを持つ連続な区分線形写像の族である。行列式が0の場合、その非線形ダイナミクスのすべては1次元の第1帰還写像によって捉えられる。この写像は、各断片が一定の帰還時間に対応する不連続な区分線形写像となる。本論文では、標準形が反発的なフォーカス不動点を持つとき、第1帰還写像の構成が有理回転数によって決定されることを示した。具体的には、帰還時間の集合と写像の断片の順序が、その回転数に対するファレイ親の左右の数列の分母によって与えられる。この結果は、切り替え多様体の逆像から形成される多角形を特徴付け、ファレイ・ウェブ上での数学的帰納法を用いることで証明された。また、パラメータ空間における構成の変化を示すいくつかの曲面が、カオスから準周期またはモードロックされたダイナミクスへの分岐点となっていることを明らかにしている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08901v1.appendix: 本論文は複素ダイナミクス(complex dynamics)に関連する力学系の理論を扱っており、特に区分線形写像の構造解析やファレイ数列を用いた組み合わせ論的なアプローチが含まれています。

papers.title: Expansive solutions with prescribed asymptotics of the classical $N$-body problem
papers.summary: We consider the classical $N$-body problem with the $\frac{1}{|x|^p}$-type potential, where $p>0$. We construct hyperbolic, parabolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions with prescribed asymptotic data as $t \to+\infty$.

papers.title: Handbook of Error-Correcting Codes
papers.summary: Barcode scans, clear phone calls, reliable data storage, satellite communication, and large-scale quantum computation are all made possible by error correction. We present a handbook version of The Error Correction Zoo, a curated reference of methods for protecting classical or quantum information from errors during storage and transmission. The handbook includes descriptions of these error-correcting codes and a classification according to the symbols they use. It also catalogues relations among codes and related objects such as sphere packings, lattices, designs, groups, and classical and quantum phases of matter. The collection is intended both as a rigorous reference and as a practical aid for tracing the web of code relationships and uncovering new connections.

papers.title: Substitution groups of formal power series
papers.summary: Let $G$ be the group of power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots\in R[[x]]$ under substitution, where $R$ is a commutative ring with $1\neq 0$ of prime characteristic $p$. Given any $n\geq 1$, the subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in R\}$ is normal in $G$, and the quotient $G_n=G/K_n$ is the group of truncated polynomials over $R$ of degree $\leq n$ under substitution. In this paper, we compute the exponent of the image of $K_r$ in $G_n$, for all $r,n\geq 1$, indicating in every case a family of elements realizing this exponent.

papers.title: Towards a Bridge Layer Between Bibliographic and Formalized Mathematical Knowledge
papers.summary: Mathematical knowledge is split between bibliographic databases (e.g., MathSciNet, zbMATH Open) and formal proof libraries (e.g., Lean mathlib), preventing unified access between published results and their formalizations. We propose a relational bridge-database that aligns publication metadata with formal artifacts, providing an interoperability layer between mathematical literature and machine-verifiable proofs. We introduce a paper-level formalization score that measures how much of a publication is covered in formal systems. As a feasibility study, we show how such scores can be estimated via cross-document alignment between informal texts and Lean formalizations, enabling large-scale analysis of formalization coverage. This framework is a first step toward integrating bibliographic and formal mathematical ecosystems into scalable, machine-actionable knowledge graphs linking publications to formal proof objects.

papers.title: Generating $\psl{2}{q}$ by elements of prime orders $2$ and $p$
papers.summary: For primes $p\geq 5$, we determine those $q$ for which the projective special linear group $\psl{2}{q}$ over the finite field of order $q$ is $(2,p)$-generated -- that is, there exist two elements of $\psl{2}{q}$ of orders $2$ and $p$, respectively, that generate $\psl{2}{q}$.

papers.title: On Balance, To What Degree is Burr's Conjecture True?
papers.summary:
For many trees $T$, the Ramsey number of $T$, denoted by ${\mathcal R}(T)$, is determined by the sizes of the partition classes in its unique bipartition. In 1976, Burr proved that when $T$ has partition classes of size $t_1$ and $t_2$ with $t_1 \le t_2$, the Ramsey number is at least $\max(2t_2-1,2t_1+t_2-1)$, and conjectured that this is tight. While counterexamples have been found for some pairs $(t_1, t_2)$, a main focus of research on this problem has been determining ratios $t_2/t_1$ or bounds on the maximum degree of $T$ for which Burr's bound is either exactly or asymptotically tight.
  We essentially resolve these questions for lopsided trees. Specifically, we show that (a) there are counterexamples whenever $t_2 \ge 2t_1$, with the order of magnitude of the difference between the largest Ramsey numbers and Burr's bound being $\max \left( t_1^2/t_2, \sqrt{t_1} \right)$, and (b) for $t_2 \ge 500 t_1$, Burr's bound is tight when $Δ(T) \le t_2 - t_1$, but is off by at least $C \log t_2$ (even when $t_2 \ge 2 t_1$) when $Δ(T) \gtrsim t_2 - t_1$. In particular, this shows that Burr's bound need not hold for $t$-vertex trees $T$ with $Δ(T) \approx t/3$.

papers.title: Instability of a nonlinear oscillator with small friction and small additive noise
papers.summary: Let $λ= λ(β,σ,a,b)$ denote the top Lyapunov exponent for the linearization along trajectories of the noisy damped non-linear oscillator $\ddot{x}+β\dot{x} + ax+bx^3 = σ\dot{W}_t$, where $a$, $b$ and $β$ are all positive and $σ\neq 0$. In 2004 Arnold, Imkeller and Sri Namachchivaya stated without proof that $λ(\varepsilon^2 β,\varepsilon σ,a,b) \sim \overlineλ \varepsilon^{2/3}$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$ with $\overlineλ > 0$. This paper contains a proof of this assertion.

papers.title: Extremal Matchings and Height Functions
papers.summary: This paper studies a lattice structure for almost perfect matchings on certain planar, bipartite (plabic) graphs embedded in a disk. Postnikov's boundary measurement map, and subsequent related work, yielded that plabic graphs parameterize positroid cells within the totally nonnegative Grassmannian with the map itself given in terms of almost perfect matchings with fixed boundary condition. For finite planar bipartite graphs, Propp introduced a distributive lattice structure on their set of perfect matchings. Subsequently Muller--Speyer, provided this distributive lattice structure on the aforementioned almost perfect matchings with fixed boundary condition. Their work also identified the extremal matchings of this lattice for boundary conditions that coincide with face labels of the plabic graph given by the positroid structure. We extend this by giving an explicit construction of extremal matchings in terms of height functions and show that all possible boundary conditions of an almost perfect matching can be obtained within this construction.

papers.title: On Terwilliger $\mathbb{F}$-algebras of factorial association schemes II
papers.summary: The Terwilliger algebras of association schemes over an arbitrary field $\mathbb{F}$ were called the Terwilliger $\mathbb{F}$-algebras of association schemes in [10]. In [7], He and Jiang studied the Terwilliger $\mathbb{F}$-algebras of factorial association schemes. In this paper, we continue studying the Terwilliger $\mathbb{F}$-algebras of factorial association schemes. We get all block idempotents of the Terwilliger $\mathbb{F}$-algebras of factorial association schemes. We get the $\mathbb{F}$-dimensions, the centers, the Jacobson radicals of the block algebras of the Terwilliger $\mathbb{F}$-algebras of factorial association schemes.

papers.title: A Proof of Nash-Williams' Conjecture
papers.summary:
A central open question in extremal design theory is Nash-Williams' Conjecture from 1970 that every triangle-divisible graph on $n$ vertices (for $n$ large enough) with minimum degree at least $0.75 n$ has a triangle decomposition. In this paper, we prove this conjecture in full.
  In 2016, Barber, Kühn, Lo, and Osthus proved that if the fractional relaxation of Nash-Williams' Conjecture holds for minimum degree $cn$ for some constant $c\ge 0.75$, then Nash-Williams' Conjecture holds for any constant $c' > c$. The previously best-known bound on the fractional relaxation was due to Delcourt and Postle from 2021 with $c= \frac{7+\sqrt{21}}{14} \approx 0.82733$. This bound on the fractional relaxation has grown in importance over the years as it has been directly tied to bounds for a number of other problems in extremal design theory.
  This paper consists of three parts. In Part I, our first main result is a proof of the Fractional Nash-Williams' Conjecture: if $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $\frac{3n}{4}$, then $G$ has a fractional triangle decomposition.
  In Part II, our second main result is a Fractional Stability Theorem for Nash-Williams' Conjecture: if a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices has minimum degree close to $\frac{3n}{4}$ but no fractional $K_3$-decomposition, then $G$ is close (in edit distance) to the join of two $\frac{n}{4}$-regular graphs each on $\frac{n}{2}$ vertices. We use this to prove that if a triangle-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices has minimum degree close to $\frac{3n}{4}$ but no $K_3$-decomposition, then $G$ is close (in edit distance) to the join of two $\frac{n}{4}$-regular graphs each on $\frac{n}{2}$ vertices.
  In Part III, our final main result is a proof of Nash-Williams' Conjecture in full.

papers.title: A general bound on $R(C_k,H)$
papers.summary: In this paper, we prove that for every $k$ and every graph $H$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, the Ramsey number $R(C_k,H)$ is at most $(k-1)m+1\le km$. This settles a problem of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, which is listed as problem 34 in the graph theory collection.

papers.title: Sharp bounds on $k$-wise generalizations of oddtowns and eventowns
papers.summary:
For $\boldsymbolα = (α_1, \dots, α_k) \in \mathbb{F}_2^k$, an $\boldsymbolα$-town is a set family in which every $i$-wise intersection has parity $α_i$. Denote by $f_{\boldsymbolα}(n)$ the maximum size of an $\boldsymbolα$-town on $[n]$. The classical oddtown and eventown problems study the cases $\boldsymbolα = (1, 0)$ and $(0, 0)$, respectively. We determine the sharp asymptotics of $f_{\boldsymbolα}(n)$ for all $\boldsymbolα$, answering questions of Johnston--O'Neill and Wei--Zhang--Ge.
  We also study a symmetric variant $g_{\boldsymbolα}(n)$, in which $i$-wise intersection sizes $|F_1 \cap \dots \cap F_i|$ are replaced by $i$-wise intersection-union sizes $|F_1 \cap \dots \cap F_i| + |F_1 \cup \dots \cup F_i|$.

papers.title: Enumeration of certain subsets of uprooted trees and spherical parking functions
papers.summary: Spherical $G$-parking functions are a distinguished subset of standard monomials, arising from the skeleton ideals of the $G$-parking function ideal. Explicit spherical $G$-parking function enumeration formulas are known only in a few classes of graphs. In this paper, we consider a family of graphs $\Gl$ ($1\leq \ell \leq n-2$), obtained from the complete bipartite $K_{n+1}$ by deleting the $\ell$ edges joining vertex $1$ to the vertices in $F_\ell= \{n-\ell+1, \ldots, n\}$. The uprooted spanning trees of $\Gl-\{0\}$ are counted by the set $\UnFl$ of uprooted trees with the vertex set $[n]$ in which vertex $1$ is not adjacent to any vertex in $F_\ell$, and we establish that $|\UnFl| = (n-1)^{n-\ell-2}(n-2)^{\ell}(n-\ell-1).$ We derive this formula combinatorially and independently recover it as an application of the matrix tree theorem, obtaining some combinatorial identities as consequences. Finally, we determine the number of spherical $\Gl$-parking functions as $|\SPF(\Gl)| = (n-1)^{n-3}(n-\ell-1)^2.$

papers.title: On the maximum and negative frustration indices of graphs
papers.summary: A signed graph is a graph with signatures ($+1$ or $-1$) on its edges. A cycle is called positive if the product of its edge signatures is positive, and a signed graph is called balanced if each cycle in it is positive. The frustration index is the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes the signed graph balanced, which is considered to be a measurement of the imbalance of the signed graph. In this paper, we compare the frustration index of the all-negative signature with the maximum frustration index of all possible signatures on the unsigned graph. We classify some families of graphs into three scenarios: the all-negative signature does not maximise the frustration index, the all-negative signature maximises the frustration index non-uniquely, and the all-negative signature maximises the frustration index uniquely. For all three scenarios, we can exhibit chordal and non-chordal graphs alike. The classes we consider include apex trees, fan graphs, wheel graphs, and complete split graphs. Moreover, for the families of fan graphs and wheel graphs, we fully characterise and count the signatures maximising the frustration index. Throughout our study, we exhibit different classes of signed graphs for which the frustration index equals the number of edge-disjoint negative triangles. Moreover, as part of our study, we are able to refute three conjectures of Zaslavsky on the frustration index.

papers.title: Edge-regular graphs with non-negative curvature have polynomial growth
papers.summary: A long-standing conjecture in the emerging discrete Bakry-Émery theory asserts that bounded-degree graphs satisfying $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ have polynomial growth. In the present paper, we prove this conjecture for all edge-regular graphs, and even obtain a volume doubling estimate with a constant that depends only on the degree. This is made possible thanks to the discovery of a surprising self-improvement phenomenon, which seems of independent interest: any edge-regular graph satisfying $\mathrm{CD}(κ,\infty)$ for some $κ\in\mathbb R$ must in fact satisfy $\mathrm{CD}(κ,n)$ for some explicit, universal and optimal dimension parameter $n$.

papers.title: Exponential mixing and enhanced dissipation on the unit sphere with Rossby-Haurwitz flows
papers.summary: We exhibit a family of smooth incompressible velocity fields on the two-dimensional unit sphere such that the time evolution of any mean-free initial data passively advected by any of them is mixed exponentially fast. In the presence of molecular diffusivity, we show that the solution to the associated advection-diffusion equation experiences enhanced dissipation with optimal decay rates. Each member of this family is an alternating combination of two Rossby-Haurwitz flows with random amplitudes and constitutes a spherical analogue to the sine shear-alternating example of Pierrehumbert.

papers.title: Logistic Gene Regulatory Networks: A Modelling Framework Beyond Hill Functions
papers.summary: Boolean networks model gene regulatory networks, but extracting quantitative dynamics requires translating their logical rules into differential equations, and the sigmoidal kernel chosen carries direct biological consequences. The near-universal choice, the Hill function, sets production to exactly zero when an activator is absent, creating a spurious absorbing off-state with no biological counterpart. We develop a product-of-logistics framework in which increasing logistic functions represent activation, decreasing logistic functions represent repression, and a recursive De Morgan product formula translates an arbitrary Boolean rule into a continuous regulatory function. The translation is automatic, confines every regulatory function to the unit interval, and retains a strictly positive basal rate. Our central result is a recovery theorem: every steady state of the Boolean network reappears, for sufficiently steep response, as an exponentially stable equilibrium of the continuous model, so the translation provably refines rather than distorts the Boolean analysis. We establish global well-posedness, forward invariance, and an explicit Lipschitz constant, and prove, for the two canonical two-gene motifs, global asymptotic stability of the negative-feedback oscillator and a closed-form bistability threshold for the toggle switch. Every threshold remains a positive, measurable concentration, unlike weighted-sum logistic formulations that place repressor thresholds at meaningless negative values. The eleven-gene Traynard mammalian cell-cycle network is translated automatically: in the proliferative regime its trajectories settle onto a sustained limit cycle reproducing the Boolean cyclic attractor. Because it is purely structural, the translation applies unchanged to existing Boolean models and supports exact feedback linearisation for control.

papers.title: There are matroid toric ideals without quadratic Gröbner bases
papers.summary:
Our paper shows that if a matroid contains the Fano plane or its dual as a minor, then its toric ideal does not have any quadratic Gröbner basis. More than 25 years ago, Hibi, Herzog, and Sturmfels established a direct connection between the existence of quadratic Gröbner bases and regular unimodular flag triangulations. Our paper solves a famous question posed by Herzog and Hibi on a polyhedral reformulation for the existence of quadratic Gröbner bases: we show that the base polytopes of the Fano plane and its dual do not have regular unimodular flag triangulations which implies the main result on Gröbner bases.
  Our proof relies on several novel tools: a lemma that connects the $1$-skeleton of a lattice polytope to the lattice points in its dilations, an encoding with Boolean formulas and SAT solvers, and symmetry-breaking arguments.

papers.title: Weighted partitions with interval restrictions: exact formulas and a bivariate master identity
papers.summary: Let $a_2''(n)$ and $b_2''(n)$ be the signed partition functions introduced by Andrews and El Bachraoui for interval-restricted partitions whose parts greater than $1$ are controlled by the smallest even part and by the number of ones. We prove two conjectures for these functions. The first gives the generating function for $a_2''(n)$ as an elementary rational term plus a false theta series with periodic signs; the second asserts that the companion coefficients $b_2''(n)$ take only the values $-1,0,1,2$. The central structural result introduces an auxiliary variable $z$ recording the number of non-compulsory parts greater than $1$. We obtain closed forms for the two resulting generating functions and prove the master identity $(1+q^2)\mathcal B(z,q)-(1+q)\mathcal A(z,q)=-q^4/(1-q^3)$ using both analytic and combinatorial techniques. At $z=-1$, this identity, together with a Rogers--Fine evaluation, gives the false theta formula for $a_2''(n)$ and an explicit generating function for $b_2''(n)$. The latter formula implies the asserted coefficient range and leads to an exact coefficient description of $b_2''(n)$. We also include a direct Heine--Rogers--Fine proof of the false theta formula, ordinary and fixed-refinement consequences of the master identity, and the resulting quantum modular interpretation.

papers.title: On zero-sum polytopes: reciprocity, rigidity, and cyclic sieving
papers.summary:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $\mathsf M(G,m)$ denote the set of zero-sum sequences over $G$ of length $m$. We introduce the zero-sum polytope $\mathcal P_G$, a rational polytope of dimension $n-1$, whose lattice points encode zero-sum sequences: \[
  |\mathsf M(G,m)|=|m\mathcal P_G\cap \mathbb Z^n|. \] This naturally realizes the enumeration of zero-sum sequences as a problem in rational Ehrhart theory, which leads to a combinatorial reciprocity theorem identifying the negative evaluations of the corresponding counting quasipolynomial with zero-sum sequences of full support. Our main results establish a face-stratified rigidity for zero-sum polytopes: whenever two such polytopes have equal total lattice point counts at specific dilations, the dimension-wise open-face strata are equinumerous. Moreover, we study the natural $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$-action on $\mathcal P_G$, derive equivariant generating functions and reciprocity formulas, and obtain cyclic sieving phenomena for natural cyclic actions.

papers.title: Weighing Timed Regular Languages: The Final Step (long version)
papers.summary: The bandwidth of a timed language characterizes the quantity of information per time unit (with a finite observation precision $\varepsilon$). The asymptotic behavior of the bandwidth as $\varepsilon \to 0$ classifies timed regular languages in three classes: meager, normal, and obese. Normal timed automata have a bounded frequency of events and some non-punctual transitions, and, up to now, were the only class of timed automata for which no algorithm was available for computing their bandwidth. In this article, we compute the bandwidth of any such automaton in the form $\approxα\log{1/\varepsilon}$. Our approach reduces this problem to computing the best reward-to-cost ratio in a weighted finite graph constructed from the given timed automaton.

papers.title: Dominance and symmetry-breaking rules for the Graph Burning Problem
papers.summary: The Graph Burning Problem (GBP) is a NP-Hard combinatorial optimization problem that models the propagation of influence or contagion in a network. The propagation is represented through the metaphor of a fire spreading through the vertices of a graph. A burning process takes place in a series of discrete time-steps. At each time step, the burning process is characterized by a propagation (where burned nodes spread the fire to their neighbors), and an ignition (where one additional unburned node is chosen to become burned). The minimum number of steps required to burn all vertices of a graph defines its burning number. Literature provides integer linear programming formulations to solve the problem, but with no surprise, such approaches struggle to converge as the graph size increases. Therefore, reducing the search space explored by these formulations becomes a key point to improve performances. In this work, we study the similarities of the Graph Burning Problem with the well-known Dominating Set Problem. We propose a new formulation based on this study and apply dominance rules and symmetry-breaking techniques to reduce the search space and consequently speed up resolution time. We also introduce a perturbation of the proposed objective function, as well as a pruning rule for the perturbed model in order to further accelerate its resolution.

papers.title: Labelled Process Logic
papers.summary: This paper develops a cyclic labelled proof-theoretic framework for process logic -- an extension of dynamic logic in which formulas specify properties of execution traces rather than only final states. The main difficulty is that first-order process logic must reason about concrete computations while preserving temporal information along regular-program traces. Existing compositional calculi cover important fragments, but do not provide a complete treatment of full first-order process logic over regular programs. We address this difficulty by enriching process-logic formulas with labels that explicitly record trace and update information during derivations. Based on this construction, we define cyclic labelled proof systems for propositional and first-order process logic, respectively denoted by G3PPL and G3FOPL. We prove the soundness by using the cyclic conditions to obtain an infinite descent in a well-founded multiset ordering, and prove the completeness by showing that the labelled systems can derive the established proof rules of process logic and first-order dynamic logic. The result is a uniform framework for process logic in which for the first time, trace-based program properties and first-order computations can be handled within the same proof structure.

papers.title: Non-Isomorphic Optimal Cayley Graphs
papers.summary: We present more than seventy optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs that are non-isomorphic to previously known optimal Cayley graphs with the same degree and diameter. For each graph, we provide comprehensive data on its parameters and structural invariants. Comparison with known constructions reported by Marston Conder on the Combinatorics Wiki and in related works reveals significant differences in girth, algebraic connectivity, domination number, automorphism group structure, cycle distributions, distance-related properties, and other graph invariants. These findings show that optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs are frequently non-unique. The new examples enlarge the catalogue of known optimal graphs and provide benchmarks for investigations in degree-diameter problems, algebraic graph theory, and extremal graph theory. Since some of the graphs were identified through randomized search techniques, the collection is not exhaustive.

papers.title: Enumerating tuples of spanning trees
papers.summary: Deciding whether a graph has k-edge-disjoint spanning trees is a well-studied problem. We consider the problem of enumerating all sets of spanning trees with polynomial delay. This work is based on the alternate proof of Tutte and Nash-Williams' characterization of graphs with k edge-disjoint spanning trees by Kaiser [1]. The idea is to maintain a decision tree for all forest-packs and perform a Depth-First Search over it. We build this decision tree inductively by computing each node's children using a variant of Kaiser's technique [1].

papers.title: Spectral Koopman Approach for Reconstructing State-space Geometry of Cislunar Restricted 3-Body Problem
papers.summary: In this work, we propose a novel approach, based on the path integral formulation of Koopman spectrum, to discover the phase-space geometry of the planar Cislunar Restricted 3 Body Problem (CR3BP). In contrast to existing techniques, which use trajectory-based (usually) local analysis, we leverage the Koopman operator framework, which generates a global linear \emph{representation} of the system, to reconstruct the global phase space geometry of the CR3BP. In particular, we compute the principal eigenfunctions of the Koopman operator via the path integral approach and show how the zero level curves of these eigenfunctions encode the phase space characteristics of the planar CR3BP.

papers.title: On the Complexity of the Bi-infinite Post Correspondence Problem
papers.summary: In the bi-infinite Post Correspondence Problem ($\Z$PCP), it is asked whether the same bi-infinite word can be constructed correspondingly from a given finite set of pairs of words. In this article, we study its complexity with respect to the arithmetical hierarchy and prove that it is in $\Si^0_2 \setminus (Π^0_1 \cup \Si^0_1)$ and, therefore, at the level 2 of the arithmetical hierarchy. For the proof, we present a sequence of reductions starting from the nonhalting of the Turing machine all the way to $\Z$PCP via infinite PCP, an $s$-shift infinite PCP and $s$-shift $\Z$PCP for all natural numbers $s$. In the process, we prove that the infinite PCP is undecidable for injective morphisms, and that the infinite injective PCP, $s$-shift infinite PCP, $s$-shift $\Z$PCP and the non-termination problem for (deterministic and reversible) semi-Thue systems are all $Π^0_1$-complete.

papers.title: Balanced Sperner families via the topological Tverberg theorem
papers.summary: For every prime power $r\ge 2$, we show that any Sperner family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with $|\mathcal F|\ge (r-1)n+1$ contains $r$ pairwise disjoint nonempty subfamilies whose unions are all equal and whose intersections are all equal. For $r=2$, this confirms a conjecture of Hegedüs, with the sharp threshold $n+1$. In this purely combinatorial problem, our proof combines a multilinear polynomial method, a continuity argument, and the topological Tverberg theorem.

papers.title: Finite free convolution via reproducing kernels and squarefree algebras
papers.summary: We give a structural account of the finite free convolutions of Marcus, Spielman, and Srivastava in terms of reproducing kernel inner products on polynomial spaces and a multilinear model over the squarefree algebra. In this model, additive convolution becomes algebra multiplication, and the nilpotent logarithm linearizes it, recovering the finite free cumulants of Arizmendi and Perales. This perspective leads to a class $\mathcal{LC}_n$ of multilinear polynomials characterized by nonpositivity of higher-order cumulants, closed under additive convolution and satisfying several key permanence properties associated with negatively dependent measures. We show that every graph Laplacian pencil belongs to this class, with higher-order cumulants given by Hamiltonian cycle counts in induced subgraphs.

papers.title: Topology and Euler characteristics of tropical varieties
papers.summary: We study Euler characteristics of tropical subvarieties of tropical abelian varieties. We prove that every H-regular subvariety, locally modeled on tropicalizations of sufficiently well-behaved very affine varieties, has nonnegative signed Euler characteristic. This gives a tropical analogue of a theorem of Green-Lazarsfeld for subvarieties of complex abelian varieties. The main input is a local vanishing theorem for H-regular tropical fans, which also yields a Lefschetz-type theorem for affine H-regular tropical varieties. We further show that the signed Euler characteristic inequality fails for general tropical subvarieties of tropical abelian varieties, and we construct a 3-dimensional tropical fan whose link is not homotopy equivalent to a bouquet of 2-spheres.

papers.title: The sharp threshold for Hausdorff convexification under Minkowski addition
papers.summary: The Dyn-Farkhi conjecture asserts that the square of the Hausdorff distance from a compact set to its convex hull is subadditive with respect to Minkowski addition. The conjecture is elementary in dimension 1, was recently proved by Meyer in dimension 2, and was disproved in dimensions $n\geq3$ by Fradelizi, Madiman, Marsiglietti, and Zvavitch. The symmetric case $A=B$, however, remained open. We show that the conjecture already fails in this restricted setting. More precisely, for every $n\geq3$, we construct a compact set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ such that $$d(A(k))=d(A)>0$$ for every $1\leq k\leq n-1$, where $d(X)$ is the Hausdorff distance from $X$ to its convex hull and $A(k):=\frac1k (A+\dots+A)$ is the $k$-fold iterated Minkowski average of $A$. We also prove that the threshold $k=n$ is sharp: for every nonempty compact $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\geq 2$, we have $$d(A(n))\leq \left(1-\frac{n-1}{n(2n-1)}\right)d(A).$$

papers.title: Accelerating NeurASP with vectorization and caching
papers.summary: Neurosymbolic AI combines neural networks with symbolic programs to create robust and explainable predictions. One such framework is NeurASP, which trains a neural network to predict concepts and reasons over them using rules written in answer set programming (ASP) to solve downstream tasks. Crucially, labels are only provided for the downstream prediction produced by the symbolic rules, not for the latent concepts themselves.Backpropagation through the non-differentiable ASP component requires expensive probability and gradient calculations, which has hindered scalability to more sophisticated tasks.In this paper, we address the current limitations of NeurASP by improving its computational performance through vectorization, batch processing and caching of intermediate computations during training. We compare computation speeds between the original and our new implementation of NeurASP and report speedups of multiple orders of magnitude for larger tasks. To this end, we propose a new dataset of difficult tasks involving playing cards, which we use to test the capabilities of NeurASP's enhanced learning function.

papers.title: Generating functions for aggregation and fragmentation: review
papers.summary: In this work, we review and revisit the generating function techniques that provide exact analytical solutions for aggregation and fragmentation equations across several physical regimes including spontaneous and collisonal shattering. For discrete coagulation-fragmentation equations with size-independent rates under monodisperse initial conditions, we show the derivation of sevaral explicit closed-form solutions. We also briefly report the exact solutions for continuous, three-particle, $D$-particle collisions and two-component generalizations. Source-driven aggregation yields steady distributions featuring a universal $s^{-3/2}$ power-law decay and a cutoff mass scaling $s_{*} \sim t^{2}$.

papers.title: Index perturbation of signed graphs
papers.summary:
Let $Γ= (G, σ)$ be a signed graph and $v$ a non-isolated vertex of $Γ$. Let $Γ-v$ denote the graph obtained by deleting the vertex $v$ together with all signed edges incident to it from $Γ$, and $d_Γ(v)$ the degree of $v$ in $Γ$. In this paper, we prove that the largest eigenvalue $λ_1(Γ)$ of $Γ$ satisfies
  \[
  λ_1(Γ) \le \sqrt{λ_1^2(Γ- v) + 2d_Γ(v) - 1},
  \]
  and we also present a refined version of this bound. Moreover, we characterize the extremal signed graphs achieving equality when $Γ$ is connected and $d_Γ(v)\ge 2$, which are switching equivalent to the balanced complete signed graph.

papers.title: Generalizing Lusztig's total positivity II : geometric properties
papers.summary: Positive structures in Lie groups with respect to a subset $Θ$ of the set of positive roots provide a generalization of Lusztig's total positivity in split real Lie groups to the setting of general real semisimple Lie groups. In [GW25] Lie groups G admitting a positive structure were classified and many key properties of the unipotent positive semigroups were established. In this article we focus on the positive semigroup in G. We establish key geometric properties of elements in the positive semigroup. Further we introduce corresponding positive and non-negative parts of flag varieties and determine the topology of the non-negative parts of flag varieties in many cases. For symplectic flag varieties we provide explicit descriptions of the positive and non-negative flag varieties.

papers.title: Beltrami problem in dimension two: local normal forms
papers.summary:
Two (pseudo-)Riemannian metrics are said to be geodesically equivalent if they share the same geodesics considered as unparametrized curves. In 1865, E. Beltrami posed the problem of describing all geodesically equivalent metric pairs locally. At generic points, this problem was solved by Dini in the Riemannian setting and later extended to the pseudo-Riemannian case by Bolsinov, Matveev, and Pucacco.
  In the present paper, we solve the Beltrami problem in dimension two by providing a complete local classification of geodesically equivalent pseudo-Riemannian metrics in a neighbourhood of a singular point. This yields a full solution of the problem in dimension two.

papers.title: Fréchet Means of Periodic Orbits in Dynamical Systems: Geometry, Dynamics, and Diagnostics
papers.summary: In many dynamical systems applications, one seeks representative trajectories summarizing families of periodic orbits arising from parameter variation or uncertainty. While the Fréchet mean provides a natural notion of averaging in nonlinear metric spaces, its application to periodic trajectories is complicated by the interplay between geometric shape and temporal dynamics. Inspired by ideas from shape analysis, we develop a framework for computing Fréchet means of periodic orbits by representing trajectories as closed curves and introducing a metric structure on a quotient space that accounts for circular phase shifts. Within this framework, we establish the existence of empirical Fréchet means in the resulting infinite-dimensional quotient space. A central finding is that the resulting Fréchet mean depends strongly on the chosen parametrization: time parametrization preserves dynamical information, whereas arc length parametrization emphasizes geometric structure. To reconcile these viewpoints, we propose a decoupled approach that computes a geometric Fréchet mean using arc length parametrization and subsequently reconstructs representative dynamics through harmonic averaging of aligned speed profiles. We further introduce curvature- and medoid-based diagnostic measures that quantify the representativeness of the resulting mean and identify situations in which averaging produces geometric artifacts or fails to capture heterogeneous ensembles. Numerical experiments for the Van der Pol oscillator, the Rosenzweig-MacArthur predator-prey model, and the Morris-Lecar neuronal model demonstrate that the proposed methodology yields robust geometric summaries together with consistent averaged dynamics. The framework provides a principled approach for constructing representative periodic trajectories and assessing their validity in uncertainty quantification and dynamical systems.

papers.title: Disjointness of rescalings of smooth area preserving flows on surfaces
papers.summary:
We consider the problem of \emph{disjointness of rescalings} $(\varphi_{κt})_{t\in \mathbb{R}}$, $κ\in\mathbb{R}$ of a flow $(\varphi_{t})_{t\in \mathbb{R}}$ in the context of smooth flows preserving a smooth invariant measure, or, equivalently, locally Hamiltonian flows on compact orientable surfaces. We show that, when the genus of the surface is $g\ge 2$, almost every locally Hamiltonian flow with 2g-2 non-degenerate simple saddles is such that any distinct two rational rescalings $(\varphi_{κt})_{t\in \mathbb{R}}$ and $(\varphi_{κ' t})_{t\in \mathbb{R}}$ with $κ=p/q$ and $κ'=p'/q'$ of different absolute values, are disjoint. Previous results on disjointness of rescalings were available only for rescalings for locally Hamiltonian flows and their special flow representations in genus one.
  The result is proved using a criterion for disjointness based on the study of the distribution of Birkhoff sums of a special representation and in particular estimates on their exponential tails decay.
  A key novel geometric ingredient in the proof is the existence of a sequence of rigidity times which display what we call bounded-type rigidity, so that a large set of points comes back in time $q$ with distance $O(1/q)$. To produce such bounded-type rigidity times we exploit a particular way of degeneration of a translation surface to a flat torus for which the vertical flow has bounded-type rotation number.

papers.title: Generalizing LCL Complexity Gaps to Unbounded Degree via Monadic Second-Order Properties
papers.summary:
The last decade of research on the LOCAL model has seen tremendous progress in understanding locally checkable labeling (LCL) problems, culminating in an almost complete classification of the possible complexities LCL problems can exhibit. In particular, on undirected trees, Chang and Pettie showed that there is no LCL problem with complexity between $ω(\log n)$ and $n^{o(1)}$ and Chang showed that, for every positive integer $k$, there is no LCL problem with complexity between $ω(n^{1/(k+1)})$ and $o(n^{1/k})$; additionally, which side of each gap a problem is found on is decidable.
  While the class of LCL problems - which, roughly speaking, consists of problems for which the correctness of a solution can be described by a finite set of allowed node configurations, which in turn can be locally verified by a constant-time algorithm - includes many important problems, it has one major restriction: problems can be defined only on bounded degree graphs, which consequently restricts all the classification and gap results mentioned above.
  In this work, we propose a generalization of LCL problems to unbounded degree using Presburger monadic second-order (PMSO) formulas; more specifically, we consider what we call Local PMSO (LPMSO) problems, i.e., problems whose correct solutions are both finitely described by a PMSO formula and locally verifiable by a LOCAL algorithm in constant time - this class contains many of the important problems studied in the LOCAL model but defines them on unbounded degree graphs. As our main result we prove that, on unbounded degree rooted trees, the aforementioned $ω(\log n)$ - $n^{o(1)}$ and $ω(n^{1/(k+1)})$ - $o(n^{1/k})$ complexity gaps (and their decidability) extend to the class of LPMSO problems.

papers.title: Continuity of projected maps of heteroclinic networks in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$
papers.summary: Stability of robust heteroclinic cycles and networks is typically studied by constructing return maps and analysing their associated transition matrices. This analysis can be simplified with the network's projected map, derived by projecting the linear action of the transition matrix onto a simplex. This projection produces a piecewise-smooth map, which is one-dimensional for heteroclinic networks in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$. We consider two such networks, the Kirk--Silber network and the $Δ$-clique network. For the Kirk--Silber network, the projected map is discontinuous on its switching manifold, while it is continuous for the $Δ$-clique network. In this paper, we address the dynamical phenomena that produce a discontinuity in the case of the Kirk--Silber network, and explain the value of the projected map at the switching manifold. We construct a completed return map near both networks, which captures the behaviour of all trajectories that begin near the network but may move away from it temporarily. We show that the discontinuity in the projected map of the Kirk--Silber network emerges due to two phenomena: first, there exists a discontinuity in a component of the completed return map in the limit as trajectories approach the Kirk--Silber network, as a result of the presence of a separatrix near the network, and, second, the procedure that defines the projected map. For the $Δ$-clique network, there is no such separatrix, and so no such discontinuity emerges. This analysis is a necessary step towards understanding the more complicated dynamics observed near heteroclinic networks of five or more equilibria.

papers.title: A sporadic strongly regular graph with parameters $(120,56,28,24)$ from a primitive action of the symmetric group on $7$ elements
papers.summary: There are up to isomorphism exactly three strongly regular graphs with parameters $(120,56,28,24)$ whose automorphism group acts primitively on the vertices. Two of these graphs belong to classical families: one is the non-orthogonality graph on anisotropic points of the hyperbolic quadric $\mathcal Q^+(7,2)$, and the other one belongs to the Johnson scheme. The third one is not well understood. In this paper, we give a description of this graph in terms of ovoids and spreads of $\mathcal Q^+(7,2)$, or equivalently in terms of overlarge sets of Steiner systems with parameters $(3,4,8)$.

papers.title: Layer Order Semantics for Automata-Based Cybersecurity
papers.summary: Layered cybersecurity pipelines transform evidence before they decide on it, and the order of those transformations determines which security facts become visible to which layer. This paper gives layer order a finite-state semantics built from a layer-order automaton, deterministic sequential security transducers, evidence markers, and a final decision automaton. The worked case is HTTP request desynchronization: front-end and back-end processors compute incompatible request boundaries, and the same trace is detected or missed according to whether framing evidence reaches the parser-differential layer before it commits. The results separate completed-trace recognition, online editing, decision synthesis, and faithful enforcement; characterize faithful online enforcement as the regular prefix-closed case under causal visibility; and show that regular policies beyond that boundary remain recognizable without becoming deployable enforcers. The framework is monolithically equivalent to finite-output deterministic edit automata, while preserving layer-local invariants such as marker birth, marker survival, and reorder-sensitive visibility. A concrete parser-pair semantics identifies the forbidden marker factor with CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE, and HTTP/2-downgrade boundary disagreement under the stated abstraction, and a contextual reorder congruence classifies which component permutations induce the same decision language. The result is an automata-theoretic account of order-sensitive security failures and a compositional vocabulary for auditing, synthesizing, and comparing layered enforcement pipelines.

papers.title: Answer Set Programming for Egg Extraction and More
papers.summary:
Three years ago, Philip Zucker posted an attempt to use answer set programming (ASP) for term extraction from e-graphs Although the task is NP-hard and ASP offers a natural modelling of e-graph terms, the initial attempt did not yield convincing results.
  From the aspect of practical ASP users, we first pinpoint the way to make ASP work and work well on the task of e-graph extraction. The initial results show the naïve ASP encoding is comparable on efficiency to the well-optimised ILP-based exact DAG extraction in the extraction-gym, and find several extra optimal extraction on the complex instances. This leads us to a further agenda: with the "better together of egg+Datalog", is there a better "better together" by having ASP as a more powerful Datalog? We discuss the potential benefit from each other.

papers.title: Quantified propositional calculi and narrow implicit proofs
papers.summary: In the implicit version of a propositional proof system Q, we work with Q-proofs that are not written down directly, but are succinctly encoded by circuits. Thus implicit Q-proofs are potentially exponentially shorter than usual Q-proofs. We study narrow implicit proofs, a restricted version of this notion, in which lines in the encoded proof can only have polynomial size. We use a cut-elimination construction to show that G_{i+1} is equivalent to narrow implicit G_i, for i >= 1, where G_i is the extension of Frege allowing reasoning with Sigma^q_i quantified propositional formulas. We show that G_1 is equivalent to implicit resolution.

papers.title: The two-sided peak polynomial
papers.summary: We derive a generating function identity for the joint distribution of the numbers of peaks of a permutation and its inverse, via enriched $P$-partitions. The coefficients of the corresponding peak polynomial $W_n(s,t)$ satisfy a second-order recurrence. A martingale formulation of this recurrence yields a bivariate central limit theorem, showing that the two statistics are asymptotically independent. We also give an exact closed form for their covariance, which is of order $n^{-1}$.

papers.title: Auto formalisation of Chaitin and of the surprise incompleteness Theorem
papers.summary:
This is a continuation of a previous report on an experiment in autoformalisation of Gödel's second incompleteness
  theorem in Agda using Claude. Using the framework built in this experiment, Claude could ``automformalise'' Chaitin's proof of the first
  incompleteness theorem and then the Kritchman-Raz surprise examination paradox version of the second incompleteness.
  As the first experiment, the project provides a case study of the strengths
  and limitations of current large language models in mathematics. Since Chaitin's proof involves coding programs, Claude had to represent
  code as ternary string and could build autonomously a parser and a continuation stack evaluation machine. The fact that we can simulate
  computations as expected is not completely trivial and we suggested a Gandy/Howard majorisation argument, that Claude had no problem to
  follow.
  The resulting formalisation clarifies a number of details left implicit in the original
  presentation and provides a fully machine-checked proof of these arguments for Church's Basic Recursive Arithmetic.

papers.title: Sets of equiangular lines in dimension $18$ constructed from $A_5^3 \oplus A_1^4$
papers.summary: In 2023, Greaves, Syatriadi, and Yatsyna found a set of $57$ equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^{18}$, breaking the previous record. In 2025, Lin, Munemasa, Taniguchi, and Yoshino constructed a large number of sets of $57$ equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^{18}$ as affine equiangular sets in an integral overlattice of $A_9^2 \oplus A_1$. In this paper, we construct further sets of $57$ equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^{18}$ from Latin squares of order $6$ and Pasch configurations, realized as affine equiangular sets in an integral overlattice of $A_5^3 \oplus A_1^4$. Unlike the previously known examples, these sets are not strongly maximal. Moreover, some of them have only five distinct Seidel eigenvalues, fewer than any previously known examples.

papers.title: Orthogonal degree-similarity of edge-deleted strongly regular graphs
papers.summary: Godsil and Sun asked whether, for a strongly regular graph $X$ and any two different edges $e$ and $f$, the edge-deleted graphs $X\setminus e$ and $X\setminus f$ are degree-similar. We give an affirmative answer to the problem of Godsil and Sun. In fact, we prove the stronger statement that if $X$ is a $1$-walk-regular graph, then for any two edges $e$ and $f$ of $X$, the graphs $X\setminus e$ and $X\setminus f$ are orthogonally degree-similar. The proof is based on an edge version of the orthogonal-intertwiner method: the equality of the Gram matrices of the projected endpoint vectors in every eigenspace yields an orthogonal matrix commuting with the adjacency matrix and sending one pair of ordered endpoint vectors to the other.

papers.title: On a Conjecture of D. B. Shapiro
papers.summary: We prove a conjecture of D. B. Shapiro, which asserts that no integral [10,10,16] formula can arise as a restriction of any Hurwitz-Radon formula.

papers.title: Beyond Explaining Predictions: Logic-Based Explanations for Confidence in Machine Learning Models
papers.summary: Machine learning is increasingly used in critical domains, where both predictions and their associated confidence levels influence important decisions. To enhance transparency in such scenarios, it is important to understand why a model is confident or uncertain about its predictions. Recent logic-based approaches provide abductive explanations, minimal subsets of features sufficient to preserve the predicted class, with correctness guarantees. However, these methods focus solely on classification behavior and may produce explanations that cover instances with low predictive confidence. In this work, we introduce the concept of Minimum Confidence Threshold (MCT), which quantifies the weakest confidence guarantee provided by an abductive explanation. Building upon this concept, we propose confidence-aware abductive explanations, which preserve not only the predicted class but also a user-specified confidence guarantee. We formulate MCT computation as an optimization problem and introduce an algorithm for generating minimal explanations that satisfy a desired confidence threshold. We evaluate the proposed framework on boosted trees for binary classification, although the approach is applicable to other machine learning models that provide confidence scores. Experimental results show that traditional abductive explanations often provide substantially weaker confidence guarantees than the confidence associated with the explained instance itself. In contrast, confidence-aware explanations consistently improve the minimum confidence guaranteed by an explanation while requiring only a modest increase in explanation length. These properties make the proposed approach particularly suitable for applications where both predictive correctness and confidence are essential for trustworthy decision making.

papers.title: Domination in Johnson graphs J(n, 3) for odd n
papers.summary: In 2025 Cornet, Dravec, and Torres determined the domination number $γ(J(n, 3))$ of the Johnson graph for every even $n \ge 6$, expressing it as a closed form $φ_n$ in terms of Fort\textendash{}Hedlund covering numbers, and conjectured the same value for odd $n$. We prove this conjecture: $γ(J(n, 3)) = φ_n$ for every odd $n \ge 7$, completing the determination of $γ(J(n, 3))$ for all $n \ge 6$.

papers.title: On the Spectra of Digraph Laplacians
papers.summary: We present several Laplacian-type matrices associated with a loopless digraph $D$: the out-/in-degree Laplacians $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}},\mathcal L_{\mathrm{in}}$, the incidence Laplacian $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{inc}}=BB^{\mathsf T}$, and the symmetrized and skew-symmetrized variants $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{out}},\mathcal K_{\mathrm{out}}$. We show that $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{inc}}(D)$ coincides with the Laplacian of the underlying undirected multigraph, and we derive spectral and characteristic-polynomial relations under arc reversal and complementation (including a simplification for Eulerian digraphs for $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{out}}$). We demonstrate that the spectral radius of $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}}$ is bounded above by the order of the digraph and give a characterization in the equality case. We further obtain explicit formulas for joins and line digraphs, giving a general determinantal identity relating the out-degree Laplacian characteristic polynomials of a regular digraph and its line digraph.

papers.title: Stabilizing Role of Uninformed Participants in Collective Decision Making
papers.summary: For groups without strict hierarchy, collective decisions often emerge through compromise. We develop a second-order network model of collective decision-making using a dissipative Hamiltonian formulation, in which informed agents introduce preferred directions while uninformed participants contribute only direction-free dissipation. We show that under low conflict, the model admits a locally unique, exponentially stable compromise state. Using a structured modular network we further show that as conflict increases the local compromise branch terminates through a saddle-node fold rather than through a smooth mean-field symmetry-breaking transition. Modular polarized states persist on branches that are locally separated from the compromise branch. Direction-free dissipation does not shift the static structural threshold, but it delays escape from the saddle-node ghost and pushes the observable onset of polarization to larger conflicts. Our work identifies a dissipation-mediated mechanism, complementary to connectivity-based accounts, through which uninformed participants stabilize collective behavior in biological and engineered swarms.

papers.title: Determination Provenance: From Ambiguity to Algebra
papers.summary: Many data systems admit multiple admissible outcomes for the same input: concurrent transactions may serialize in one of many orders; a logic program may have multiple stable models. Classical data provenance cannot even pose its question in such settings -- it explains how a result was derived, but only after something has chosen which result to produce. We introduce \emph{determination provenance} to track the commitments that resolve this ambiguity. A tuple's \emph{support} is the set of resolutions under which it holds. Supports form a commutative semiring, and layered commitments induce a \emph{filtration} measuring each tuple's \emph{query-relative depth} -- how many layers of semantic resolution it depends on. Positive relational algebra respects the filtration, enabling compositional robustness analysis and quantitative diagnosis of resolution cost. We instantiate the framework for transactional isolation and for $\mbox{Datalog}^\neg$; in both, classical semantic variants (isolation levels; negation semantics) correspond to different views of a single shared filtration.

papers.title: Dynamic E-unification
papers.summary: We present an E-unification procedure for a set of non-ground (dis)equations, along with a dynamic set of ground (dis)equations, and prove its completeness. The ground part is dynamic in the sense that it continually changes. The algorithm saturates the non-ground equations using Superposition modulo the ground theory. We also have an Instantiation rule that matches the left hand side of non-ground (dis)equations with ground terms, creating new ground (dis)equations, which changes the ground theory. This algorithm can be used in quantified SMT problems, where the dynamic ground theory represents the evolving model. We develop an ordering to compare terms modulo a ground theory, which is used to orient non-ground equations. We prove properties of this ordering, using a weak form of monotonicity and subterm property. We finally present a set of inference rules for our ordering, which allows us to properly orient equations in theories of some finite data structures, such as a theory of finite lists with length and append.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11484v1.title: 誤り訂正符号ハンドブック
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11484v1.summary: 情報の保存や伝送の際に生じる古典的または量子的なエラーを修正するための手法を網羅した、参照用リファレンス『The Error Correction Zoo』のハンドブック版。バーコードの読み取りから大規模な量子計算まで、幅広い分野における誤り訂正符号の記述と分類を提供している。また、符号と球充填、格子、デザイン、群、そして古典および量子物質相といった関連オブジェクトとの接続性を系統立てて整理しており、厳密なリファレンスかつ新たな関係性を発見するための実用的なガイドとなっている。
keywords: Classical and quantum phases of matter
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11484v1.appendix: 本論文は符号と群の関連性について整理しているため、興味ある分野に含まれる「structure of large countable infinite group」に関連する可能性があります。また、符号の構成における組合せ論的側面は「combinatorics on words」などの分野とも関連を持ちます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11461v1.title: 形式的べき級数の代入群
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11461v1.summary: 素標数 p の可換環 R 上の代入演算に関する形式的べき級数群 G と、その正規部分群 Kₙ = {x + aₙ₊₁xⁿ⁺¹ + aₙ₊₂xⁿ⁺² + ... | aᵢ ∈ R} による商群である n 次の切断多項式群 Gₙ = G/Kₙ について研究している。本論文では、すべての r, n ≥ 1 に対し、商群 Gₙ における Kᵣ の像の指数 (exponent) を決定し、その指数を与える具体的な元の族を提示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11461v1.appendix: この論文は「structure of large countable infinite group」に関連する内容を含んでいます。形式的べき級数のなす代数的な群構造を扱っており、その有限次元の商群における性質を詳細に分析しているためです。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11335v1.title: 極値マッチングと高さ関数
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11335v1.summary: 本論文は、ディスク内に埋め込まれた特定の平面二部グラフ（plabic graph）における概完全マッチングの束構造を研究している。Posnikovの境界測定写像やその後の研究により、plabic graphは全非負グラスマン多様体内のポジトロイド・セルをパラメータ化し、その写像は固定された境界条件を持つ概完全マッチングによって記述されることが知られている。有限平面二部グラフについては、Proppが完全マッチングの集合上に分配束構造を導入し、後にMullerとSpeyerがこれを境界条件を固定した概完全マッチングへと拡張した。本研究では、この束の極値マッチングを高さ関数を用いて明示的に構成する手法を提案し、概完全マッチングにおけるすべての可能な境界条件がこの構成から得られることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11335v1.appendix: この論文は、平面二部グラフの組み合わせ論的構造やその束構造を扱っており、[興味ある分野]の中では combinatorics に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11137v1.title: 根無し木（uprooted trees）の特定の部分集合と球面パーキング関数（spherical parking functions）の数え上げ
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11137v1.summary: 本論文では、完全二部グラフ Kₙ₊₁ から頂点 1 と特定の頂点集合 F_ℓ = {n-ℓ+1, ..., n} を結ぶ ℓ 本の辺を削除して得られるグラフの族 Γ_ℓ (1 ≤ ℓ ≤ n-2) を対象に、その根無しスパニング木の数および球面 Γ_ℓ-パーキング関数の数を特定している。まず、頂点 1 が F_ℓ のどの頂点とも隣接しない根無し木の数 |U_{n, F_ℓ}| を (n-1)ⁿ⁻ˡ⁻²(n-2)ˡ(n-ℓ-1) と導出した。この公式は、組合せ論的手法および行列木定理（matrix tree theorem）の両方を用いて証明されており、副次的にいくつかの組合せ論的恒等式も得られている。最終的に、球面 Γ_ℓ-パーキング関数の総数が |SPF(Γ_ℓ)| = (n-1)ⁿ⁻³(n-ℓ-1)² であることを明らかにした。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11137v1.appendix: 本論文はグラフ理論および組合せ論に関する研究であり、提示された興味ある分野の中では「combinatorics on words」に関連する基礎的な数え上げ技術や、離散構造の組合せ論的解析という側面で関連性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11094v1.title: 非負の曲率を持つ辺正則グラフは多項式成長する
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11094v1.summary: 離散Bakry-Émery理論における長年の予想である「CD(0, ∞)を満たす次数有界グラフは多項式成長する」という命題を、辺正則グラフのクラスにおいて証明した。本論文では、次数のみに依存する定数を持つ体積倍増推計（volume doubling estimate）を導出している。この成果は、CD(κ, ∞)を満たす辺正則グラフが、実際にはある明示的かつ最適な次元パラメータnに対してCD(κ, n)を満たすという「自己改善現象（self-improvement phenomenon）」の発見に基づいている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11094v1.appendix: 本論文で扱われているグラフの成長（polynomial growth）に関する性質は、提示された興味ある分野のうち「structure of large countable infinite group」における群の成長特性や幾何学的性質の研究と理論的な関連性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11028v1.title: ロジスティック遺伝子制御ネットワーク：Hill関数を超えたモデリングフレームワーク
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11028v1.summary: 本論文では、ブーリアンネットワーク（BN）の論理規則を微分方程式へ変換するための新しいフレームワークとして、ロジスティック関数の積を用いた手法を提案している。従来のHill関数を用いたモデルでは、活性化因子が不在の際に生成率が完全にゼロになるという、生物学的に不自然な吸収状態が生じる問題があった。これに対し、本手法ではロジスティック関数の積とド・モルガンの法則に基づく再帰的公式を用いることで、任意のブーリアン規則を、厳密に正の基礎生成率を持つ連続的な制御関数へ自動変換する。数学的成果として、BNのすべての定常状態が、十分な急峻さを持つ応答の下で連続モデルの指数安定な平衡点として再現される「回復定理」を証明した。また、哺乳類の細胞周期ネットワーク等の具体例を通じて、リミットサイクルの再現や双安定性の閾値の導出、制御のための正確なフィードバック線形化への応用可能性を示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11028v1.appendix: 本論文は、ブーリアン規則という離散構造から微分方程式という連続力学系を構築する手法を扱っており、複素力学系（complex dynamics）や記号力学系（symbolic dynamics）の概念的基盤である離散と連続の対応関係に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11003v1.title: 時間正規言語の重み付け：最終段階（ロングバージョン）
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11003v1.summary: 時間言語の帯域幅（bandwidth）は、有限の観測精度 ε の下での単位時間あたりの情報量を特徴付ける。ε → 0 における漸近的挙動に基づき、時間正規言語は meager、normal、obese の3つのクラスに分類される。本論文では、これまで帯域幅の計算アルゴリズムが存在しなかった normal クラスの時間オートマトンに対し、その帯域幅を ≈ α log(1/ε) の形式で算出する手法を提示する。この手法は、与えられた時間オートマトンから構築された重み付き有限グラフにおける、最適な報酬対コスト比（reward-to-cost ratio）を求める問題へと帰着させるものである。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11003v1.appendix: 本論文は興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」および「formal languages」に強く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10966v2.title: グラフ・バーニング問題に対するドミナンス規則および対称性の破れの規則
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10966v2.summary: グラフ・バーニング問題（GBP）は、ネットワークにおける影響力の伝播や感染をモデル化したNP困難な組合せ最適化問題である。各時間ステップにおいて、燃焼済みのノードからの延焼（propagation）と、新たな未燃焼ノードへの着火（ignition）を繰り返し、全頂点を燃やすための最小ステップ数である「バーニング数」を求める。本論文では、GBPと支配集合問題（Dominating Set Problem）の類似性を調査し、それに基づいた新しい定式化を提案した。さらに、探索空間を削減して計算を高速化するために、ドミナンス規則や対称性の破れ（symmetry-breaking）の手法、目的関数の摂動、および枝刈り規則を導入している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10966v2.appendix: 本論文はグラフ理論および離散最適化を扱っており、指定された興味ある分野の中では「combinatorics（組合せ論）」に密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10961v1.title: ラベル付きプロセス論理 (Labelled Process Logic)
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10961v1.summary: 本論文は、実行トレースの性質を記述する動的論理の拡張であるプロセス論理に対し、循環的なラベル付き証明論的枠組みを構築している。正則プログラムのトレースに沿った時間的情報を保持しつつ具体的な計算を扱うため、ラベルを用いてトレースと更新の情報を明示的に記録する手法を導入した。命題レベルのG3PPLおよび一階レベルのG3FOPLという2つの循環ラベル付き証明体系を定義し、整礎多重集合順序における無限降下法を用いて健全性を、既存の体系との比較により完全性を証明した。これにより、トレースに基づくプログラム特性と一階の計算を統一的な証明構造で扱えるようになった。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10961v1.appendix: 本研究は正則プログラムやトレースといった概念を扱っており、オートマトン理論 (automata theory) や形式言語 (formal languages) の論理的基礎に関わりがあります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10930v1.title: 両側無限ポストの対応問題の計算量について
