The main consequences of this construction are that the free non-degenerate bijective solution to the Yang--Baxter Equation in the catego\-ry~$\mathcal{RNS}_n$ has a solvable Word Problem, and that every law holding in for finite solution of the previous type also holds for {\it every} solutions of the same type.
  In the remainder of the paper, we present further explicit realizations of free objects and explore their consequences. Among these are free two-sided skew braces of abelian type (with abelian multiplicative group) and free centrally nilpotent skew braces of class $2$.

papers.title: An infinite family of counterexamples to a question of Camina
papers.summary: A.R. Camina and R.D. Camina posed in \cite{camina06} the following question: Suppose there are two finite groups, one nilpotent and the other non-nilpotent, and the two groups share identical sets of conjugacy class sizes; must the non-nilpotent group possess a non-trivial center? Recently, W. Zhou \cite{zhou25} gave a negative answer via a subtle and elegant construction of concrete counterexamples. Nevertheless, his approach relies on the existence of Sophie Germain primes, and thus fails to yield infinitely many counterexamples unconditionally. In the present paper, we construct an infinite family of counterexamples to Camina's question.

papers.title: Formalizing a Many-Sorted Hybrid Polyadic Modal Logic in Lean
papers.summary:
We present a Lean formalization of a general hybrid modal logic with many-sorted signatures and polyadic modal operators. The system borrows ideas from both algebraic specification and dynamic logics, and is designed to serve as a uniform axiomatic foundation for specifying and verifying programming languages and security protocols. We expose a DSL for users to define languages and protocols as many-sorted signatures, specify the relevant domain-specific axioms, and reason about program executions or protocol runs. We provide a machine-checked proof of its soundness theorem and showcase the framework's versatility through several applications: an imperative programming language for code verification, the BAN logic for security protocols, and the modal system S5. We have designed our formalization to be intrinsically sorted, that is, well-sorted formulas in the base language are well-typed terms in Lean. Thanks to intrinsic sorting, all domain specific applications can be easily embedded in our framework via the DSL, at no additional syntactic overhead required for the user to prove.
  All code presented in this paper is openly accessible in the following repository: https://github.com/alexoltean61/msphml-lean

papers.title: On the independence of the slow and fast scales in multiple-scale expansions, with application to Van der Pol's equation
papers.summary: When implementing the method of multiple scales, one is traditionally instructed to treat the slow and fast time scales as if they were independent. Despite the intuitive motivation and the effectiveness of this perturbation method, one cannot failt to notice that these two scales relate to the same unique variable, so independence can only be formal. How sensible is it, then, to split a variable asymptotically into two (or more) independent ones? In this paper, we elucidate this issue with Van der Pol's equation, one of the simplest weakly nonlinear oscillators, as well as a simple example of a Hopf bifurcation. The discussion involves carrying the multiple-scale analysis up to arbitrarily large order and dealing with the divergent character of the resulting asymptotic series. Using the technique of optimal truncation, we re-connect the two scales. Specifically, we show that an initial translation of the fast coordinate leads to a non-trivial, exponentially small, phase shift that depends on the slow coordinate. This phase shift breaks the independence of the slow and fast scales and is found to result from the nonlinearity. Numerical simulations confirm its existence, as well as the predicted scaling. The calculation is carried out in sufficient detail to provide confidence in the generality of our result, both in its essence and in its form. In particular, we find strong indications that a Hopf bifurcation with a quadratic nonlinearity would lead to the same phenomenon, but with a larger magnitude.

papers.title: Averaged Fourier Estimates and Dyadic Approximation on the Cantor set
papers.summary: Let $C$ be the middle-third Cantor set and let $μ$ be the natural Cantor probability measure. Let \[ γ=\frac{\log2}{\log3}. \] The two main results of this paper are \[ μ\{x\in C:\|2^n x\|<n^{-τ}\text{ for infinitely many }n\}=0 \qquad \text{ for } τ>2-γ. \] and \[ μ\{x\in C:\|2^n x\|<n^{-τ}\text{ for infinitely many }n\}=1 \qquad \text{ for } τ<\frac{1-γ}{2}. \] These results give new progress toward Velani's conjecture on zero-one law for dyadic approximation in the middle-third Cantor set.

papers.title: Cusp Excursions, Lattice Points on Manifolds, and the Mizohata-Takeuchi Conjecture
papers.summary: We prove new logarithm laws for cusp excursions in spaces of lattices, and produce quantitative lower bounds for lattice points near submanifolds, using tools from dynamics and the geometry of numbers. As an application, we provide a new proof of power loss for the local Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture with explicit error terms, as well as show that power loss is generic in $C^k$. The construction uses high-dimensional probabilistic estimates, but replaces the random orthogonal subspaces of Cairo-Zhang with random unimodular lattices; this yields stronger bounds and provides a richer family of counterexamples.

papers.title: Hidden critical and Morse equivalence behind duality: Theory and Applications
papers.summary:
The aim of this paper is to establish critical duality theory for ratios of nonnegative homogeneous convex functions (shorten for RC functions) and differences of convex functions (abbreviated as DC functions) on Banach spaces. Specifically, we establish a series of duality results on critical point theory and Morse theory for RC functions, including the homotopy type of sublevel sets, the Morse critical points and their Rothe critical groups, Lagrange critical points and their multiplicities, Lusternik-Schnirelman min-max critical values, Poincare polynomials, as well as the structure of handlebody decompositions, all of which are proved to be preserved under polarity dual. Moreover, we obtain the first critical duality theory of DC functions which does not depend on the DC decomposition. This answers a question left open from the work of Toland on DC functions and the work of Le-Pham on DC programming.
  We apply these results to provide a reformulation of the graph Cheeger constant using zonotopes; we introduce the contact data which serves as a geometric characterization of Lagrange criticality; and we show that the eigenproblems for 1-Laplacian and $\infty$-Laplacian on hypergraphs are equivalent to the contact problems of zonotopes, which indeed establishes a new characterization of zonotopes. We also prove a duality equivalence for certain nonlinear eigenvalue problems and bifurcation problems. Our study here reveals an intricate interaction of critical point theory with other fields such as convex analysis, combinatorial geometry, and nonlinear eigenproblems on graphs.

papers.title: Proof of Cigler's conjecture on $q$-Hoggatt numbers
papers.summary: We prove the nonnegativity and palindromicity of a family of polynomials arising from $q$-Hoggatt numbers. The nonnegativity is derived from Stanley's $(P,ω)$-partition theory through a standard Young tableau formula, while the palindromicity is proved by an involution on rectangular standard Young tableaux. Our result confirms a conjecture of Cigler.

papers.title: Non-Uniform and Weighted Crossing Gates in Two-Dimensional Sandpiles
papers.summary:
Determining whether predicting two-dimensional sandpiles lies in $\mathbf{NC}$ or is $\mathbf{P}$-complete has been open for decades. Moore and Nilsson proved $\mathbf{P}$-completeness for the three dimensional case by encoding Boolean circuits into sandpiles, but this method fails in two dimension due to the impossibility of crossing gates.
  In this work, we study the existence of crossing gates on non-uniform and weighted grids. We establish an equivalence between uniform weighted crossing gates and a class of simple non-uniform crossing gates, which we call primal. We also exhibit a crossing gate that inherently requires more than one crossing, rather than a single crossing as in standard constructions. Finally, we show that the equivalence between uniform weighted and primal crossings breaks down in more general settings.

papers.title: Onsager--Machlup functionals for McKean--Vlasov SDEs via Euler-type approximation
papers.summary: The Onsager--Machlup action functional provides a variational framework for characterizing the most probable transition paths of stochastic systems and plays an important role in the study of nonequilibrium fluctuations. Its extension to McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations is complicated by the intrinsic distribution dependence of the coefficients. In this paper, we address this difficulty by introducing an Euler-type approximation scheme based on classical, distribution-free stochastic differential equations. Combining the classical Onsager--Machlup theory with a convergence argument for the approximation sequence, we derive an explicit expression for the Onsager--Machlup functional associated with the McKean--Vlasov SDE. The proposed approach is constructive and extends to a broad class of distribution-dependent stochastic systems.

papers.title: On Lefschetz's point-free periodicity
papers.summary: We motivate two new approaches to the study of Lefschetz point-free periodicity. The first focusses on spaces satisfying the Wecken property. As an example, we study the bubble spaces. The second is a relative study of the Lefschetz point-free periodicity. This becomes important, for example, in the study of repellers of dynamical systems.

papers.title: Construction of Lyapunov density for nonautonomous dynamical systems on hypertorus
papers.summary: We present a semidefinite programming framework for constructing time-varying Lyapunov densities for nonautonomous dynamical systems on a hypertorus. The formulation leverages Gram matrix representations of hybrid (real-trigonometric) polynomials. In addition, we introduce a novel block decomposition of these Gram representations to confine the blow-up of the resulting density to a prescribed set. The results are then applied to establish the almost global synchronization of a time-varying Kuramoto model and the robust almost-global stability of a parameter-varying nonautonomous system. These examples demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method and validate the theoretical results. All computational results are obtained using an open-source MATLAB implementation, as referenced in the text, thereby facilitating reproducibility of the reported examples.

papers.title: On Periodic Geodesics of Half-Lie Groups
papers.summary: A central program in infinite-dimensional Riemannian geometry is to understand which classical finite-dimensional principles remain valid beyond finite dimensions. In this article, we study the existence of periodic geodesics on Hilbert half-Lie groups equipped with strong right-invariant Riemannian metrics. Building on recently established completeness results for this class of infinite-dimensional manifolds, we prove that every nontrivial free homotopy class contains a periodic geodesic whenever the fundamental group is nontrivial. We further establish a Lyusternik-Fet type theorem in this setting. Assuming a Palais-Smale condition modulo right translations and the existence of a nontrivial higher homotopy group, we prove the existence of a nonconstant contractible periodic geodesic. Thus, as in the finite-dimensional setting, both first and higher homotopy information continue to force the existence of periodic geodesics in infinite dimensions. In addition, we describe a reduction principle based on compact finite-dimensional totally geodesic submanifolds and apply our results to groups of Sobolev diffeomorphisms equipped with right-invariant Sobolev metrics.

papers.title: Groups of type $\mathrm{E}_8$ over rings via TKK-algebras and their extremal elements
papers.summary: Over any commutative ring containing $\tfrac16$, we study Lie algebras $L$ of type $\mathrm{E}_8$ that arise from the Tits--Kantor--Koecher (TKK) construction on a Brown algebra, and their twisted forms. We construct a smooth scheme $\mathbf{Y}$ of pairs of extremal elements in $L$. When $L$ arises from the TKK-construction, we express the automorphism group, of type $\mathrm{E}_8$, as an $\mathrm{E}_7$-torsor over $\mathbf{Y}$. We show that twisting by this torsor produces the graded isomorphism classes of those algebras isomorphic to $L$, and parametrize these classes by using $\mathbf{Y}$. We show that this torsor is non-trivial, yielding isomorphic Lie algebras of type $\mathrm{E}_8$ that are not graded isomorphic, as opposed to the behaviour over fields.

papers.title: Avalanche homology of digraphs via sandpile dynamics
papers.summary: We introduce avalanche homology as a new (di)graph homology theory, based on the dynamics of the sandpile model. Avalanche homology is the simplicial homology of the avalanche complex generated from the sets of unstable vertices at the time steps of the sandpile dynamics. In this work we focus on digraphs, and our main results give the homotopy types of the avalanche complex for directed paths and directed cycles for certain initial configurations of the sandpile dynamics. Even for such simple digraphs a wide range of topologies can arise, and we compare this to the directed flag complex and to the recently introduced burning homology. Furthermore, the dynamics yields very naturally a filtered simplicial complex, and hence persistent avalanche homology.

papers.title: Artin monoids, their homomorphisms and twins
papers.summary: Motivated by the twin homomorphism problem for Coxeter groups and the corresponding Hecke monoids, we find a large class of its solutions originating from standard homomorphisms of Artin monoids and their compositions. These homomorphisms are expected to be injective when they are optimal and injective on generators, which generalizes the homogeneous homomorphisms and the famous Tits conjecture recently settled by Paris. We classify disjoint standard homomorphisms and conjecture the complete classification when the domain is of rank two.

papers.title: Complementing Emerson-Lei Elevator Automata (Technical Report)
papers.summary: Büchi elevator automata naturally appear in several areas of formal methods as a structural expressibly-equivalent subclass of Büchi automata where every strongly connected component is either deterministic or inherently weak. It was shown that this class contains the majority of Büchi automata generated in practical applications, including LTL model-checking and verification of hyperproperties. Moreover, the elevator subclass enables more efficient complementation and determinization algorithms than unrestricted Büchi automata. In this paper, we introduce Emerson-Lei elevator automata, which is a generalization of Büchi elevator automata to richer acceptance conditions. We provide a complementation algorithm with a significantly better asymptotic complexity than the best known algorithm for unrestricted Emerson-Lei automata. The practical efficiency of our algorithm is demonstrated by an experimental comparison with the popular state-of-the-art tool Spot. Our work is, to the best of our knowledge, the first step towards practical algorithms for complementing, determinizing, and testing universality and inclusion of Emerson-Lei automata with rich acceptance conditions.

papers.title: Effective Resistance-Based Graph Sparsification and Community Detection
papers.summary: Community detection is a key task in network analysis, providing insight into the structural organization of complex systems. Effective resistance, a graph-theoretic metric derived from electrical network theory, has emerged as a powerful tool for evaluating connectivity and influence within networks. This paper proposes an effective resistance-based community detection algorithm that calculates the similarity between nodes using effective resistance values and produces a weighted graph. The sparse graph used in the algorithm is generated after computing the minimum spanning tree (MST) of the weighted graph and adopting a threshold sparsification strategy on non-MST edges. A maximum modularity approach is adopted using the Clauset-Newman-Moore algorithm on the resultant sparse graph. This algorithm is evaluated for both synthetic and real-world networks, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to popular existing methods. The result shows that the effective resistance-based approach accurately captures the structures of the community while maintaining computational efficiency.

papers.title: Maximum Forest Number of General Bipartite Graphs: Structural and Complexity Results
papers.summary: Recent results established the maximum forest number $f(B)$ for balanced bipartite graphs under Ore-type degree sum conditions. In this paper, we extend these results by determining the exact value of the maximum forest number as a closed-form formula for general bipartite graphs under Ore-type conditions, answering an open question posed by Yu. We prove that the maximum forest number is bounded by a discrete optimization over at most six critical structural coordinate points dictated by hyperbolic density constraints. Furthermore, we establish that deciding whether a specific balanced bipartite graph on $2n$ vertices has a forest number of at least $n+2$ is NP-complete. This implies that while the maximum possible forest number can be exactly bounded, computing the exact forest number for a given graph remains computationally intractable, and a simple structural characterization via finite forbidden induced subgraphs cannot exist unless P = NP.

papers.title: Dimension Spectrum of Continued fraction Expansions with Coefficients restricted to the Fibonacci Sequence
papers.summary: In this paper, we analyze the structure of the dimension spectrum of continued fraction expansions with coefficients restricted to the generalized Fibonacci sequence. Let $F_{(a_1,a_2)}$ denote the generalized Fibonacci sequence starting with the positive integers $a_1<a_2$. We prove that the continued fractions whose digits lie in $F_{(a_1,a_2)}$ have full dimension spectrum for every $(a_1,a_2)$ such that $a_1 \geq2$, or $a_1=1$ and $a_2\geq3$. On the other hand, using the numerical tools developed by Falk and Nussbaum, we show that the dimension spectrum has a gap for continued fractions with digits restricted to each of the sets $F_{(1,2)}$ and $F_{(2,1)}$, where $F_{(2,1)}$ denotes the set of Lucas numbers. Moreover, for $F_{(1,2)}$ and $F_{(2,1)}$, we prove that the dimension spectrum always contains a non-trivial interval.

papers.title: Strong counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture in every uniformity
papers.summary:
The classical supersaturation problem, originating in classical results of Rademacher and Erdős on complete graphs, asks for the minimum number of copies of an $r$-graph $\mathcal{F}$ in an $n$-vertex $r$-graph with $\ex(n,\mathcal{F})+q$ edges. Mubayi conjectured that, for every stable non-$r$-partite $r$-graph $\mathcal{F}$, this minimum is at least $q c(n,\mathcal{F})$, where $c(n,\mathcal{F})$ is the minimum number of copies created by adding one edge to the $n$-vertex extremal $\mathcal{F}$-free $r$-graph. Ma and Yuan recently constructed infinitely many graph counterexamples, with arbitrary chromatic number at least four.
  We construct, for every $r\ge 2$ and every $K>1$, a stable non-$r$-partite $r$-graph $\mathcal{F}$ with the following property: for all sufficiently large $n$ and every integer $q$ with $1\le q\le δn$, there is an $n$-vertex $r$-graph with $\ex(n,\mathcal{F})+q$ edges and at most $K^{-1}q c(n,\mathcal{F})$ copies of $\mathcal{F}$. Thus Mubayi's conjectured lower bound can already fail at $q=1$, and the failure can be by an arbitrarily large constant factor in every uniformi

papers.title: The Model Checking Problem for Distributed Knowing How is $Δ^p_2$-Complete
papers.summary: We investigate the complexity of the model checking problem for distributed knowing how. We show that the problem is $Δ^p_2$-complete.

papers.title: Algorithmic Foundations of Deep Learning: Complexity-Theoretic Rates and a Characterization of Universal Approximation
papers.summary:
Feedforward neural network (NN) expressivity is typically studied by emulating optimal basis-expansion schemes. While powerful, this perspective is incomplete: it primarily captures complexity through regularity, and therefore does not distinguish intuitively simple and complicated objects with comparable regularity, such as the square-root function and a typical Brownian path.
  The guiding message is that neural networks should be viewed not only as flexible basis functions, but also as models of computation. If a function is computable by a real-valued circuit over a prescribed elementary gate language, then it can be computed to comparable accuracy by an NN with explicit depth, width, and non-zero-parameter bounds controlled by the depth, width, gate count, and gate structure. Thus, neural-network complexity is not governed by regularity alone, but also by algorithmic complexity. We then show that any definable NN model satisfying a natural parallelization condition, allowing possibly multivariate non-linearities such as attention or layer normalization, is a universal approximator if and only if it contains a non-affine nonlinearity.
  The scope of our theory is illustrated by deducing universal approximation guarantees for continuous functions, minimax-optimal approximation guarantees for Besov classes, logarithmic-error complexity for holomorphic functions, and by showing that NNs can emulate numerical algorithms such as Newton-Raphson root finding and power iteration without architecture-specific arguments. Its precision is illustrated by shortest-path computation on $k$-vertex graphs: compiling the tropical dynamic-programming circuit yields NNs with O(log(1/ε)) non-zero parameters, exponentially improving in 1/ε over the generic $O(ε^{-c k^2})$ Lipschitz-approximation scale, for a constant c>0.

papers.title: An algebraic study of ideals of weak graph homomorphisms
papers.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be finite simple graphs and assume that either both are undirected or both are directed. We introduce and study the ideal of weak graph homomorphisms $I_{G\to H}$. We characterize all graphs $G$ and $H$ for which every (equivalently, some) power of $I_{G\to H}$ has a linear resolution. Moreover, unmixedness, Cohen-Macaulayness, projective dimension and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of these ideals are studied.

papers.title: How Can Size and Ceiling Bounds Affect the Complexity of Nonuniform Automata Families?
papers.summary: In the past literature, families of two-way finite automata and pushdown automata having limited state complexity (i.e., the total number of inner states) and stack-state complexity (i.e., the total number of inner states multiplied by the total number of strings "pushable" to a stack), have been studied in direct connection to (mainstream)  space-bounded complexity classes equipped with Karp-Lipton style advice of limited size when all inputs given to the automata have bounded length. Here, we acknowledge two major factors -- size and ceiling -- of such families, which have a significant impact on the complexity of finite and pushdown automata families, where the "size" refers to (stack-)state complexity and the "ceiling" refers to an input's length bound. In this line of study, we further explore those effects caused by different sizes and ceilings.

papers.title: Parallel Communicating Finite Automata: The Non-Forgetting Model
papers.summary: Parallel Communicating Finite Automata (PCFA) are systems of several finite automata that can communicate by requesting the state of another automaton. As an attempt to make PCFA as defined in [8] and [2] more realistic, the non-forgetting model is introduced where automata retain their own states while querying. As in previous publications, several variants of these automata systems are considered. The computational capacity of the non-forgetting model is investigated and compared to ''forgetting'' systems and multi-head finite automata. It is shown that most variants of non-forgetting PCFA are as powerful as multi-head automata in the deterministic and nondeterministic cases where the number of automata equals the number of heads. The only exception is the special case of deterministic centralized systems in non-returning mode. Here, a strict inclusion is proved. In the course of this proving, a proof from [2] is completed. With that, this paper answers some questions for nfPCFA that are open for the classical ''forgetting'' case.

papers.title: On some Open Problems for Finite Automata with Translucent Input Letters
papers.summary:
Finite automata with translucent input letters are a recent model of discontinuous input processing. Basically, classical finite automata are equipped with a translucency function that defines, depending on the state, the set of translucent input symbols. While processing the input, translucent symbols are skipped and only visible symbols are read and processed. It is distinguished between deterministic and nondeterministic models and, in addition, between returning and non-returning models. In the former case, the automaton restarts from the left end of the input after having consumed some visible symbol, whereas in the latter case the automaton restarts from the left end of the input when the right endmarker symbol is seen.
  Returning finite automata with translucent letters have been introduced by Nagy and Otto and its non-returning variant has been introduced by Mraz and Otto. Many results concerning the computational capacity, relations between deterministic and nondeterministic models, and relations between returning and non-returning models are known. Moreover, some results on closure properties and decidability questions have been obtained as well. However, some questions have still been open since many years. In this paper, we will give answers to some of these open questions.
  In particular, we show the non-closure under concatenation, Kleene star, reversal, and inverse homomorphism for the non-returning deterministic as well as nondeterministic model. We also obtain non-closure under inverse homomorphism for the returning deterministic and nondeterministic model. Finally, we investigate the emptiness problem for non-returning finite automata with translucent input letters and show the decidability of the problem in case of deterministic as well as nondeterministic automata.

papers.title: Idefix-Free Languages and Their Application in External Contextual Grammars
papers.summary: In this paper, we continue the research on the power of contextual grammars with selection languages from  subfamilies of the family of regular languages.  We investigate infix-, prefix-, and suffix-free languages (referred to as idefix-free languages) and compare such language families to some other subregular families of languages (finite, monoidal, nilpotent, combinational,  (symmetric) definite, ordered, non-counting,  power-separating, commutative, circular, union-free, star, and comet  languages). Further, we compare the families of the hierarchies obtained for external  contextual grammars with the language families defined by these new types for the selection. In this way,  we extend the existing hierarchies by new language families.

papers.title: 2-Head 2D Returning Finite Automata
papers.summary: We introduce and study a family of two-head finite automata called  two head returning finite automata (2-HRFA) operating on rectangular arrays of picture languages, in which both heads move in opposite directions. We show that the class of picture languages accepted by 2-HRFA is incomparable with the class of languages generated by context-free matrix grammars (CFMG), while it forms a proper subset of the class of languages accepted by returning pushdown automata (RPDA). In addition, we define a constrained variant, both head stepping two head returning finite automata (B2-HRFA), in which both heads are required to move in a synchronized, stepwise fashion. We prove that the class of languages accepted by  returning finite automata (RFA) is a proper subset of the class of languages accepted by B2-HRFA, which in turn is a proper subset of the class of languages accepted by 2-HRFA. Closure properties for both the families of languages accepted by 2-HRFA and B2-HRFA are also investigated.

papers.title: Efficient Regex Matching with Sparse Counting-Sets
papers.summary: Regular expressions with counting operations (c-regexes) offer a compact representation of repeating patterns by allowing numerical bounds to be added to subexpressions. Recent work introduced the counting-set data structure, which allows simultaneous updates of multiple counter values for efficient matching. However, this approach suffers from a performance bottleneck when counting-sets must be replicated due to the presence of branching transitions. We propose a sparse counting-set approach, which reduces the replication overhead by maintaining only essential counter values, thereby yielding a more efficient matching algorithm.

papers.title: Selective Memoization for Efficient Backtracking Regular Expression Matching
papers.summary: Backtracking regular expression matchers are widely used due to their expressive power but may exhibit exponential worst-case matching time. Memoization provides a principled method for eliminating redundant computation and ensuring linear matching time, but full memoization is memory-intensive and impractical. We introduce the Minimum Feedback Node (MFN) memoization scheme, a selective memoization strategy based on computing a minimum feedback vertex set of an automaton. We establish relationships with existing memoization schemes and analyze their behaviour under both Thompson and Glushkov automaton constructions.

papers.title: How Long Can the Escaping Ant Be Confined?
papers.summary:
Langton's ant is a simple two-dimensional cellular automaton whose long-term behavior exhibits remarkable complexity. While it is known that the ant eventually escapes any finite connected region of the grid, the quantitative aspects of this escape remain poorly understood. In this paper, we study the escaping time of Langton's ant, defined as the maximum number of steps the ant can perform within a finite connected domain before leaving it.
  We establish general upper bounds on the escaping time as a function of the domain size, and derive improved bounds for rectangular domains. In particular, we obtain a factorial upper bound for square domains via an inductive decomposition argument. We also obtain linear upper bounds for rectangular domains of height two and three via a column-by-column analysis. More generally, for rectangular domains with a fixed height, we establish a polynomial upper bound in the number of columns. These results are complemented by exact values computed through an optimized simulation algorithm that exploits the geometric symmetries of the grid and employs a backtracking branching strategy to avoid exhaustive search over all color configurations. We also provide lower-bound constructions, proving that the linear upper bounds for rectangular domains of heights two and three are asymptotically optimal.

papers.title: A geometric approach to inner problems associated with exponentially small splitting phenomena in local bifurcations
papers.summary: In this paper, we study analytic nonlinear partial differential equations for $\mathbf y=\mathbf y(x,θ)\in \mathbb C^n$ of the form $x^2 \mathbf y'_x(1+\mathcal O(x)) + \mathbf y'_θ+x \mathbf A \mathbf y = \mathcal O(x^2)$, $()'_z=\frac{\partial}{\partial z}$, $z=x,θ$, with $x\in \mathbb C$ and $θ\in \mathbb C /(2π\mathbb Z)$ denoting the independent variables. We show that solutions are $1$-sums (with respect to $x$) of Fourier series with coefficients of type Gevrey-$1$. The motivation for studying these equations is that so-called inner problems, associated with two-dimensional formal connections in unfoldings of local bifurcations, can be brought into this form (by looking for invariant manifolds in blowup coordinates). In the present paper, we give two examples: The zero-Hopf bifurcation and the resonant Hopf-Hopf bifurcation. Importantly, these inner problems are given by the unperturbed problem (i.e. at the bifurcation) and the invariant manifolds are expressed directly in phase space (through blowup coordinates associated with the local bifurcation). This contrasts the Lazutkin-based formulation of inner problems which is based upon a blowup of singularities (with respect to complex time) of approximate solutions; for local bifurcations this requires (artificial) coordinate transformations. We solve the PDE by extending the Banach-convolution-algebra-approach to Borel-Laplace by Bonckaert and De Maesschalck (2008) to account for analytic Fourier series. In further details, we apply the Borel transform with respect to $x$ (keeping $θ$ fixed) and solve the resulting equation in an appropriate Banach space of Fourier series with coefficients that have exponential growth in the Borel plane. The solutions of the PDE are then obtained through application of the Laplace transformation.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Size Transfer for Neural ODEs on Sparse Random Graphs: Graphon Limits and Adjoint Convergence
papers.summary: Graph Neural Differential Equations (GNDEs) model continuous-time graph dynamics by parameterizing Neural ODE velocity fields with Graph Neural Networks. Their local, size-independent filters suggest a zero-shot size-transfer principle: train on a small graph and deploy on larger, similar graphs without retraining. We develop a quantitative theory for this principle on sparse random graphs sampled from graphons. We consider Graphon Neural Differential Equations (Graphon-NDEs) and adjoint Graphon-NDEs as the infinite-node limits of the forward and adjoint GNDE systems, and establish well-posedness. For an $n$-node random graph with sparsity parameter $α_n$, we prove trajectory-wise convergence of GNDE solutions to Graphon-NDE solutions at rate $O((α_n n)^{-1/2})$, up to logarithmic factors, with high probability. We also establish uniform-in-time convergence bounds for adjoint systems governing hidden-state and parameter gradients. We further study discretize-then-optimize (DTO) and optimize-then-discretize (OTD) training. Under explicit Euler discretization with $M$ steps, we show that DTO and OTD are asymptotically consistent, with hidden-state and local parameter-gradient discrepancies of orders $O(1/M)$ and $O(1/M^2)$, respectively, up to sparsity and logarithmic factors. Experiments on HSBM and tent graphons support the theoretical rates, while zero-shot transfer experiments across four graphon classes demonstrate accurate deployment of learned GNDEs on larger independently sampled graphs.

papers.title: Fast Enumeration of Minimal Removable Sets in Monotone Systems with Application to Core Collapse Analysis
papers.summary: In network vulnerability analysis, it is crucial to evaluate the robustness of $k$-cores against vertex removals. A $k$-core is often fragile since removing a few vertices can trigger a large reduction in the core size, a phenomenon known as core collapse. In this paper, we study the problem of enumerating all minimal removable sets (MinRSs) of a given $k$-core, where a MinRS is a minimal nonempty set of vertices whose removal results in a smaller $k$-core graph. We consider this problem within a general mathematical framework based on monotone systems. We show that, for a monotone system that is given with an underlying graph $G=(V,E)$, all MinRSs of a solution can be enumerated in $O((n+m)nτ_ω)$ time, where $n=|V|$, $m=|E|$ and $τ_ω$ denotes the computation time of evaluating the monotone function of the system. Furthermore, if the system satisfies the newly defined in-dominating seed property, the complexity drops to $O((n+m) \log n \cdot τ_ω)$ time. We prove that standard $k$-cores in undirected graphs satisfy this property, enabling MinRS enumeration in $O((n+m)\log n)$ time, a significant improvement over the baseline. We also extend our framework to enumerate all solutions in a given monotone system. This yields an $O((n+m)\log n)$-delay algorithm for all $k$-core subgraphs, outperforming an algorithm given by [Boley et al., Theoretical Computer Science, 2010]. Our framework is applicable to various $k$-core extensions, including weighted $k$-cores, multi-layer $\boldsymbol{k}$-cores, and $(k,\ell)$-cores.

papers.title: A multiplicative ergodic theorem in random and simultaneous dynamics
papers.summary: In this manuscript, we consider finitely many maps defined on a compact probability space; each of which preserves the probability measure. We consider two aspects of growth of dynamical systems in this scenario; the first setting where we let some infinite lettered word determine the path through which the orbit of points evolve, while the second setting where we consider all possible paths through which the orbit of a set may evolve. Our aim in this paper is to provide a full description of the celebrated multiplicative ergodic theorem, originally due to Oseledets, for such dynamical systems that is point-valued (as in the first case) and set-valued (as in the second case).

papers.title: Bricks in which every vertex is incident with a forcing edge
papers.summary: An edge of a matching covered graph G is a forcing edge if it lies in precisely one perfect matching of G. A matching covered graph is a brick if and only if it is 3-connected and bicritical (the deletion of each pair of distinct vertices results in a graph with a perfect matching). In this paper, we prove that every vertex of a brick is incident with a forcing edge if and only if the brick is an odd wheel up to multiple edges.

papers.title: The longest and shortest roots of a real cubic
papers.summary: There are many formulas in the literature providing roots of a real cubic that avoid some of the well-known pathologies of Cardano's formulas. Among these, we identify two that consistently provide the unique roots of a depressed cubic that have the greatest and smallest absolute value, whenever those exist. We call these the longest and shortest roots. The existence conditions are elementary and are in terms of the signs of the coefficients and the discriminant. Our proofs use two algebraic identities satisfied by hypergeometric functions; once the standard real branches are fixed, the root comparisons are entirely real. As an application, the longest-root formula gives an explicit factorization of all but a vanishing proportion of depressed real quartics.

papers.title: Time Structure in Infinite Extensive Games
papers.summary: We extend graph theoretic characterizations of time structurable extensive games from finite informational digraphs to countable and continuum digraphs built on continuum rooted real trees. Introducing the symmetric class quotient poset of information sets as the canonical object an external clock must order, we develop a theory of transitive reduction for these quotients and prove existence and uniqueness under an interval finiteness condition. Under natural topological regularity assumptions like closed reachability classes, order density, and sigma compactness, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for real valued time labelings and construct measurable selection procedures in Polish spaces. We also provide constructive algorithms and a differential game example illustrating applications and computational implications.

papers.title: Classification of regular Cayley maps of skew-type three on semidihedral groups
papers.summary: It is well known that every regular Cayley map $M = \CM(G,X,p)$ on a finite group $G$ with respect to an inverse-closed generating set $X$ of $G$ and a specified cyclic permutation $p$ on $X$ corresponds to a skew morphism $\varphi$ on $G$ such that the restriction of $\varphi$ to $X$ is $p$. The skew-type of the map $M$ is defined as the index $[G:\Ker \varphi]$, which equals the number of distinct values in $\mathbb{Z}_{|\varphi|}$ taken by the associated power function $π$ of the skew morphism $\varphi$. In this paper, we develop a covering theory of skew morphisms and as an application we provide a classification of regular Cayley maps of skew-type three on the semidihedral groups.

papers.title: Characterizing Pure Strategy Nash Equilibria in Finite Noncooperative Games
papers.summary: The classical existence result of Nash guarantees that every finite noncooperative game admits an equilibrium in mixed strategies, but it leaves open the question of when pure strategy equilibria exist. This paper develops a structural approach to that question by exploiting properties of the best-response correspondence on finite strategy sets. Building on recent work, we derive new sufficient conditions for the existence of pure strategy Nash equilibria in finite games. We introduce several broad classes of finite games for which pure equilibria are guaranteed, including a class that generalizes unilaterally competitive games and a class characterized by the existence of an aggregate-payoff maximizer over an ordered set. Our results clarify the role of acyclicity, and aggregation in producing pure equilibria and connect disparate sufficient-condition results in the literature into a unified framework.

papers.title: Theory-Scale Auto-Formalization of Logics for Computer Science
papers.summary: Auto-formalization is critical for scalable formal verification, but existing progress largely focuses on isolated statements, while theory-scale auto-formalization, which coherently translates hundreds of interdependent definitions, lemmas, and theorems, remains open due to challenges in consistency, faithfulness, scalability, and correctness. In this paper, we introduce LCS-Bench, a stand-alone, theory-scale benchmark based on Logics for Computer Science. LCS-Bench is built through a novel semi-automated agentic pipeline that leverages concept graphs, formal signature planning, issue tracking, sorry-filling with counter-example search, complemented by faithfulness review from human experts. The resulting artifact covers 327 textbook items, over 4,076 Lean declarations, and more than 85K lines of Lean code. The dataset supports broad evaluation through a data engine that automatically derives five tracks of evaluation benchmarks, measuring different aspects of auto-formalization and theorem-proving capabilities. We also introduce a novel evaluation protocol featuring definitional equivalence checkers, enabling more fine-grained and faithful assessment. Through extensive evaluation on 14 models, we demonstrate that (1) LCS-Bench is of high quality, consistent, and faithful; (2) the benchmark is challenging, with state-of-the-art models achieving only 20.1% on auto-formalization tasks; and (3) our analysis reveals key findings regarding theory-scale auto-formalization and suggests promising directions for future work.

papers.title: The Suda-Tanaka-Tokushige conjecture for $\mathbf{p}$-biased intersecting families
papers.summary:
In 2017, Suda, Tanaka and Tokushige conjectured that if $1>p_1\ge\cdots\ge p_n>0$ with $p_3\le \frac{1}{2}$, then every intersecting family $\mathcal A\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ satisfies $μ_{\mathbf{p}}(\mathcal A)\le p_1$, where $μ_{\mathbf{p}}$ is the non-uniform product measure defined by $μ_{\mathbf{p}}(\mathcal{A})=\sum_{A\in\mathcal{A}} \prod_{i\in A} p_i \prod_{j\in [n]\setminus A}(1-p_j)$. In addition, if $p_1 > p_3$ or $p_1 < \frac{1}{2}$, then equality holds if and only if $\mathcal{A}$ is a star centered at some $i \in [n]$ with $p_i = p_1$. In this paper, we prove this conjecture in the following stronger $t$-intersecting form: for any $t\ge 1$, if $p_{t+2}\le \frac{1}{t+1}$, then every $t$-intersecting family $\mathcal{A} \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ satisfies
  $μ_{\mathbf{p}}(\mathcal A)\le \prod_{i=1}^t p_i$. Moreover, when $p_{t+2}<\frac{1}{t+1}$, equality holds if and only if $\mathcal{A}=\{A\subseteq [n]: T\subseteq A\}$ for some $T\in \binom{[n]}{t}$ with $\prod_{i\in T} p_i=\prod_{i=1}^t p_i$. Our result unifies and generalizes the classical theorems of Fishburn-Frankl-Freed-Lagarias-Odlyzko and Friedgut.

papers.title: On the sum of the two largest eigenvalues of the curl-curl operator on graphs
papers.summary:
The Grone--Merris conjecture, proved by Bai in~2011, states that the spectrum of the graph Laplacian $Δ_0 = -\operatorname{div}\operatorname{grad}$ is majorized by the conjugate of the vertex degree sequence. Duval and Reiner proposed a simplicial complex analogue of this statement. On a graph, where triangles serve as $2$-simplices, their conjecture reduces to the assertion that the spectrum of $\operatorname{curl}^*\operatorname{curl}$ is majorized by the conjugate of the second-order degree sequence, which records the number of triangles containing each vertex.
  We prove that the sum of the two largest eigenvalues of $\operatorname{curl}^*\operatorname{curl}$ does not exceed the sum of the first two entries of that conjugate sequence. This confirms the first two majorization inequalities predicted by Duval and Reiner for $\operatorname{curl}^*\operatorname{curl}$. As a corollary, we obtain upper bounds for the two largest eigenvalues of the full graph Helmholtzian $Δ_1 = -\operatorname{grad}\operatorname{div} + \operatorname{curl}^*\operatorname{curl}$. The same result extends to the up-Laplacian of any $3$-family, yielding a concrete step towards the Duval--Reiner conjecture in dimension~$1$.

papers.title: Structural Properties and Applications of the Augmented Sombor Index
papers.summary: Topological indices are key quantitative descriptors in mathematical chemistry, unchanged under symmetry operations and retaining graph connectivity; they capture molecular structural features to provide insights into molecular stability and chemical properties, becoming indispensable in cheminformatics and theoretical chemistry. Among degree-based indices, the \textbf{Sombor index} is widely concerned for capturing structural information, and motivated by enhanced structural discrimination, the \textbf{augmented Sombor index} ($ASO$) is defined for a connected graph $Ω$ with $|V(Ω)|\geq 3$ as $$ASO(Ω) = \sum_{v_iv_j\in E(Ω)} \sqrt{\frac{d_i^2 + d_j^2}{d_i + d_j - 2}},$$ where $d_i$ and $d_j$ are the degrees of vertices $v_i$ and $v_j$, respectively. Within the scope of this study, we first establish several sharp bounds for the augmented Sombor index and characterize the extremal graphs attaining these bounds. In particular, we determine the minimum value of the $ASO$ index for unicyclic graphs with a prescribed girth and characterize all graphs achieving this minimum. We also identify the second maximum $ASO$ value among trees and characterize the corresponding extremal tree structures. Furthermore, the minimum and maximum values of the $ASO$ index for bipartite graphs and chemical graphs are obtained, together with a complete characterization of the associated extremal graphs. In addition, we characterize the chemical trees that maximize the $ASO$ index. The chemical applicability of the $ASO$ index is investigated through quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) analysis, supported by a comparative assessment of several variants of the Sombor index. Finally, we present concluding remarks and outline potential directions for future research on the augmented Sombor index of graphs.

papers.title: Order-2 bygone-state opacity of labeled finite-state automata
papers.summary: In this paper, we formulate a scenario that an agent can never be sure that another agent can uniquely determine the state of a finite-state automaton based on its observations to the automaton at the current and any past time as the property of order-2 bygone-state opacity. Based on our concurrent composition and the classical observer, we derive a tool to verify this property in doubly exponential time. The interest of this result lies in that we extend inference of finite automata from a single agent to two ordered agents.

papers.title: Learning Probabilistic Filters with Strictly Proper Scoring Rules
papers.summary: Bayesian filtering of partially and noisily observed dynamical systems seeks to infer the evolving conditional distribution of the state of a dynamical system, given observations, in an online fashion. This Bayesian filtering distribution is the natural object for uncertainty quantification, but it is rarely available as a supervised learning target. However, one can often use the forecast model to generate synthetic system trajectories, along with synthetic observations. We introduce the proper scoring ensemble filter (PSEF), an ensemble data assimilation method based on training an analysis map to approximate the filtering distribution using only synthetic state--observation trajectories. The analysis step is represented as a permutation-invariant, transformer-based map that takes as input a forecast ensemble and observations, producing an analysis ensemble. Training is based on strictly proper scoring rules -- with the energy score used in our implementation -- so that probabilistic accuracy is rewarded over the whole probability distribution. We prove that, under a realizability assumption, the population objective is minimized by the true Bayesian filtering distribution. We also derive the finite-ensemble empirical objective used in training and relate its single state--observation trajectory form to the population objective, using a mean-field consistency argument. Numerical experiments show that the learned filter accurately approximates challenging filtering distributions, including nonlinear, non-Gaussian, and multi-modal posteriors, and achieves stronger performance in data assimilation tasks than classical methods or learning-based methods with mean-squared-error objectives. For close-to-Gaussian problems, learning a correction to the EnKF is the best approach, while for highly non-Gaussian problems an end-to-end approach that discards this inductive bias is superior.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Specifications for VeriFast
papers.summary: Static verification tools can assure industrial scale software, but require significant human labor to write specifications. This is particularly true of static verifiers based on separation logic (SL verifiers), which excel at verifying heapmanipulating programs, but require many complex auxiliary specifications to reason about heap structure. Recent work applies large language models (LLMs) to generate code, tests, and proofs, including specifications for verifiers, but mostly targeting non-SL verifiers. To address this gap, this paper thoroughly evaluates how well LLMs perform when prompted to generate specifications for verifying 303 C functions with the SL verifier VeriFast. We explored eight prompting approaches, ten LLMs, and three input types in two stages. Quantitative and qualitative analyses are used to assess the LLM-generated code and specifications for functional behavior, verifiability and errors. The results show that LLMs preserve functional behavior in source code and specifications (both over 91%), but achieve modest verification success (31.4%). Using Gemini 2.5 Pro and providing formal contracts lead to higher success rates in our setting. Moreover, most errors (94%) come from LLMs' mistakes in the domainspecific knowledge of SL verifiers such as VeriFast. These findings provide guidance for optimizing LLM-generated specifications for SL verifiers.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27272v1.title: 放物型に有界な primitive な繰り込みにおける MLC
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27272v1.summary: 本論文では、繰り込みのタイプが primitive であり、かつマンデルブロ集合 M のカスプに接近し得るような無限回繰り込み可能なパラメータのクラスに対して、ア・プリオリな評価および MLC（マンデルブロ集合の局所連結性）を証明した。そのために、繰り込みの退化を制御するための様々な手法（Thin-Thick 分解、Value Calculus、Wanderers 定理、Wave 補題など）を開発・洗練させている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27272v1.appendix: 本論文は complex dynamics（複素力学系）の分野と密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27209v1.title: 確率的双模倣距離の連続性について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27209v1.summary: ラベル付きマルコフ連鎖における確率的双模倣距離は、遷移確率の摂動に対して不連続となることがあり、実測データに基づくモデルへの適用を困難にしている。本論文では、以前に距離0における連続性の十分条件として提案された robust probabilistic bisimilarity が、必要条件でもあることを証明した。さらに、非双模倣的な状態ペアに対しても頑健性の概念を拡張することで、確率的双模倣距離の連続性に関する完全な特徴付けを与えた。この理論的成果に基づき、連続性を判定する多項式時間アルゴリズムを開発し、実験評価によって、連続性の判定が距離自体の計算に対して極めて低い追加コストで実行可能であることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27209v1.appendix: ラベル付きマルコフ連鎖や計算モデルの等価性を扱うという点で、automata theory と関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27198v1.title: アメナブル群の捻れ群C*-環とその包含関係に対するselflessness
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27198v1.summary: 本論文では、Robertの意味でのselflessnessという性質が、離散アメナブル群Gの捻れ群C*-環 C*_r(G, σ) においてどのような条件下で成立するかを論じている。特に、無限かつ有限生成なvirtually nilpotent群Gにおいて、これが(G, σ)がKleppnerの条件を満たすことと同値であることを示した。また、より広範なFC-hypercentral群のクラスに対しては、Z-安定性（または有限核次元）の条件下で同様の結果を得ている。さらに、正規部分群Hに対する包含関係 C*_r(H, σ') ⊆ C*_r(G, σ) について、相対的Kleppner条件を用いたselflessnessの特徴付けを行い、アメナブル群やvirtually nilpotent群における具体的な成立条件を導出している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27198v1.appendix: 興味ある分野のうち、「structure of large countable infinite group」に強く関連しています。具体的には、virtually nilpotent群やFC-hypercentral群といった特定の無限群の構造的性質が、その捻れ群C*-環の代数的性質（selflessness）にどのように帰着されるかを記述しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27172v1.title: 木トポロジー上のパラメータ化検証について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27172v1.summary: ランデブー同期を伴う有限状態プロセスのパラメータ化検証は、プロセスが線形順序である場合には決定不能であることが知られている。本論文では、木トポロジーにおける安全性確認の計算複雑性を、2種類の制限を設けることで特定した。木の深さを制限する場合、複雑性は急成長階層（fast growing hierarchy）に関連する。また、木における上方向と下方向の同期の交互切り替え（フェーズ）回数を制限する場合、フェーズ数が固定であればEXPSPACE完全、入力の一部であれば2EXPSPACE完全（いずれも深さは任意）となることが示された。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27172v1.appendix: 本論文は「automata theory」および「formal languages」の分野に関連しています。有限状態システムの安全性検証や計算複雑性の解析は、これらの分野における中心的なトピックです。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27170v1.title: ℬ-admissibleおよび関連するサブシフトの自己同型について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27170v1.summary: 本論文では、KimとRoushがソフィ・サブシフトの自己同型群の研究で開発した手法を拡張し、サブシフトが巨大な自己同型群を持つための十分条件を導出している。この手法を倍数集合によって定義される非ソフィ・サブシフトに適用し、特にℬ-admissibleサブシフトにおいて、その自己同型群が自明であるか、あるいはフルシフト{0,1}ᶻの自己同型群を埋め込みとして含む（巨大である）かという二分法を確立した。さらに、ℬが無限集合かつ無限の互いに素な部分集合を持たない場合、ℬ-freeサブシフトの遺伝的閉包の自己同型群が巨大であることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27170v1.appendix: 興味ある分野のうち、symbolic dynamics、structure of large countable infinite group、および倍数集合を扱う性質からarithmetic dynamicsに関連する研究です。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27166v1.title: VASにおける半線形帰納的不変式の前方のみによる構成
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27166v1.summary: ベクトル加算システム (VAS) の可到達性問題に対し、非可到達性が常に半線形帰納的不変式によって証明可能であることを利用した、新たな前方のみの構成手法を提案する。従来の不変式構成は、ソースとターゲットの両方に依存する双方向的な手法であったが、本手法はソース構成のみから不変式を構築することで、システム構造をより反映した標準的な不変式の取得を可能にする。この手法は周期的VASに対して周期的帰納的不変式を生成し、分岐VAS (Branching VAS) への拡張に向けた重要な一歩となる。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27166v1.appendix: 本論文は興味ある分野のうち、automata theory および formal languages に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27148v1.title: Hypercups: 2面より多くの状態を持つカップの反転問題
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27148v1.summary: Man-Keung SiuとIan Stewartによる2010年の研究『n個のカップを一度にm個ずつ反転させる方法』を拡張し、カップがk ≥ 2個の状態を持つ「k-hypercups」を定義した。従来の2状態（正立・倒立）のパズルはパリティに依存していたが、本論文では、k-hypercupsにおける反転の可否は最大公約数（GCD）に依存することを示した。SiuとStewartの先行研究のすべての結果をk-hypercupsへと一般化しており、従来の結果を包含する理論体系を構築している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27148v1.appendix: この論文は、離散的な状態遷移と可到達性を扱う点で combinatorics on words や automata theory の分野と関連があります。パリティから最大公約数への一般化は、代数的組合せ論の視点からも興味深い内容です。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27104v1.title: Pinwheel Schedulingにおける密度閾値予想の証明
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27104v1.summary: Pinwheel Scheduling問題とは、各タスクiに正の整数の周期aᵢが割り当てられ、各タスクをaᵢ日以内に少なくとも1回実行するようにスケジュールする問題である。本論文では、ChanとChinが1993年に提唱した、密度（各タスクの実行レート1/aᵢの総和）が5/6以下であれば常にスケジュール可能であるという予想を証明した。証明の手法として、問題を分数周期へと適切に一般化することで、有限個のケースに対する計算機探索へと帰着させている。また、2種類の異なる周期を持つ密度1以下のインスタンスの可スケジュールの証明や、Bamboo garden trimming問題に対する近似比4/3の高速なアルゴリズムも副産物として導出している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27104v1.appendix: 本論文は、スケジュールの記号列としての性質を扱う点において「combinatorics on words」の分野に関連があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27085v1.title: 双曲群のcommensuratorにおける平均的な歪み
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27085v1.summary: 幾何学的に剛性（rigid）を持ち、かつ剰余有限（residually finite）な双曲群において、そのcommensurator（共測化群）が有界な平均的な歪み（average distortion）を持つことを証明している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27085v1.appendix: この論文は「structure of large countable infinite group（巨大な可算無限群の構造）」の分野に深く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27075v1.title: 正則グラフ上の離散時空波動核とトレース恒等式
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27075v1.summary: 本研究では、(q+1)正則グラフ X におけるアフィン・ラプラス型作用素に関連した離散時空波動方程式を考察しています。前進時間差分スキームに対して、離散変形ベッセル関数と X 上の non-backtracking walk 数を用いた2つの波動核の明示的な公式を導出し、波動伝播とグラフの組合せ論的データの直接的な関係を明らかにしました。さらに、波動核の一意性を利用してアフィン・ラプラス型作用素に関する新しいトレース型公式を証明し、三角関数の和や二項係数を用いたチェビシェフ多項式の有限和に関する様々な組合せ論的恒等式の導出に応用しています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27075v1.appendix: 本論文は、グラフ上の組合せ論的構造と作用素の関連性を扱っており、[興味ある分野]の中では combinatorics に密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27074v1.title: 代数的デーン充填を用いたGromov-Thurston多様体の判別
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27074v1.summary: Gromov-Thurston多様体のホモトピー型を判別するための基準を開発しました。このアプローチは、多様体の基本群を相対的双曲群のバーチャルなデーン充填として記述することに基づいています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27074v1.appendix: 本論文は基本群の構造を扱っており、興味ある分野のうち「structure of large countable infinite group」に関連があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27062v1.title: ジャンプ、インタラクション、および交差型について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27062v1.summary: DanosとRegnierによって提案されたJumping Abstract Machine (JAM)は、GirardのGeometry of Interactionに基づくInteraction Abstract Machine (IAM)の最適化であり、Hyland-Ongのゲーム意味論の構文的な対応物であるPointer Abstract Machine (PAM)と同型である。本論文では、これらを一般化したParametric Jumping Abstract Machine (PaJAM)を導入し、非冪等交差型(non-idempotent intersection types)との密接な対応を明らかにした。PaJAMのバックトラッキングの深さを0に固定するとJAM/PAMを、無制限にするとIAMを再現できる。また、型理論的な手法を用いてPaJAMの計算量を解析し、バックトラッキングの深さが有限の範囲において、弱頭部β簡約のステップ数に対して多項式的であり、妥当なコストモデルとなることを示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27062v1.appendix: 本論文で扱われる抽象機械の動作や計算量の解析は、広義にはオートマトン理論(automata theory)の基盤的な側面と関連性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27056v1.title: 自由歪ブレースとYang--Baxter方程式の自由解
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27056v1.summary: 本論文では、Yang--Baxter方程式の自由な非退化双射解の構造歪ブレースが自由であることを証明し、冪零解の圏(RNSₙ)においても同様の結果を示しています。任意のクラスの自由右冪零歪ブレースの実用的な構成法を提示し、その自由オブジェクトが自由な加法群および乗法群を持つこと、また特定の条件下で残留有限かつホップ的であることを明らかにしました。この構成の主な帰結として、圏RNSₙにおける自由な非退化双射解の語の問題(Word Problem)が可解であることや、特定のタイプの有限解で成り立つ法則が同タイプのすべての解でも成立することを証明しています。さらに、アーベル型の自由両側歪ブレースやクラス2の自由中心冪零歪ブレースの具体的な実現についても論じています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27056v1.appendix: 本論文は「Word Problem」の可解性や「structure of large countable infinite group」に関連する群構造の性質を扱っており、興味ある分野の formal languages や代数的構造の解析に深く関わっています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27034v1.title: カントール集合における平均フーリエ推定と二進近似
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27034v1.summary: この論文は、1/3カントール集合 C とその自然な確率測度 μ における、||2ⁿ x|| < n⁻τ という形式の二進近似の性質を調査している。γ = log 2 / log 3 と定義したとき、τ > 2 - γ では無限回成立する点の集合の測度が 0 となり、τ < (1 - γ)/2 では測度が 1 となることを示した。これらの結果は、1/3カントール集合における二進近似の零一法則に関する Velani の予想に向けた新たな進展を与えるものである。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27034v1.appendix: 本論文は興味ある分野のうち、arithmetic dynamics および symbolic dynamics に関連する内容を含んでいます。カントール集合のようなフラクタル集合上でのディオファントス近似の解析は、これらの分野において重要なテーマです。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27020v1.title: 格子空間におけるカスプへの偏移、多様体上の格子点、および溝畑・竹内予想
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27020v1.summary: 本論文では、力学系と数論幾何の手法を用いて、格子の空間におけるカスプへの偏移に関する新しい対数則を証明し、部分多様体近傍の格子点に対する定量的下限を導出している。この応用として、局所的な溝畑・竹内予想における冪指数の減衰（power loss）に関する新しい証明を具体的な誤差項とともに示し、さらにCk空間において冪指数の減衰が一般的（generic）であることを明らかにした。この構成には、高次元の確率論的評価が用いられており、既存手法で用いられていたランダムな直交部分空間をランダムなユニモジュラ格子に置き換えることで、より強力な境界条件と豊富な反例の族を提供している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27020v1.appendix: 本論文は「arithmetic dynamics」の分野に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26943v1.title: 2次元サンドパイルにおける非一様および重み付き交差ゲート
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26943v1.summary: 2次元サンドパイルの予測問題がNCに属するか、あるいはP完全であるかは数十年来の未解決問題である。MooreとNilssonは3次元サンドパイルにおいて論理回路を符号化することでP完全性を証明したが、2次元では交差ゲートの構築が不可能であるためその手法は適用できない。本研究では、非一様および重み付き格子における交差ゲートの存在を調査した。その結果、一様な重み付き交差ゲートと、primalと呼ばれる単純な非一様交差ゲートのクラスとの間の等価性を確立した。また、単一の交差ではなく本質的に複数の交差を必要とする交差ゲートを提示し、より一般的な設定では一様重み付きとprimalな交差の等価性が崩れることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26943v1.appendix: 本論文は、サンドパイルモデルの計算複雑性や組み合わせ論的性質を扱っており、興味ある分野のうち symbolic dynamics や combinatorics に関連する計算理論的な側面を持っています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26877v1.title: Lefschetzのポイントフリー周期性について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26877v1.summary: Lefschetzのポイントフリー周期性の研究に向けた2つの新しいアプローチを提案している。第一のアプローチはWeckenの性質を満たす空間に焦点を当てたもので、具体例としてバブル空間（bubble spaces）を調査している。第二のアプローチは、力学系のリペラー（repellers）の研究などで重要となる、Lefschetzのポイントフリー周期性の相対的な研究である。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26877v1.appendix: 力学系のリペラーの研究に関連していることから、complex dynamicsやsymbolic dynamicsといった分野との関連性が示唆されます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26786v1.title: サンドパイル力学系を用いた有向グラフの雪崩ホモロジー
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26786v1.summary: 本論文では、サンドパイルモデルのダイナミクスに基づいた、(有向)グラフに対する新しいホモロジー理論「雪崩ホモロジー (avalanche homology)」を導入する。雪崩ホモロジーは、サンドパイルの各時間ステップにおいて生じる不安定な頂点の集合から構築される「雪崩複体」の単体的ホモロジーである。本研究では特に有向グラフに焦点を当て、特定の初期構成における有向道や有向サイクルの雪崩複体のホモトピー型を決定している。これらの単純な有向グラフにおいても多様なトポロジーが生じることを示し、既存の有向フラグ複体やバーニングホモロジーとの比較を行っている。さらに、このダイナミクスから自然にフィルター付き単体複体が得られるため、パーシステント雪崩ホモロジーへの拡張も提示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26786v1.appendix: サンドパイルモデルという離散的なダイナミクスを扱っている点で、興味ある分野の symbolic dynamics と深い関連があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26776v1.title: Artinモノイド、その準同型およびtwin
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26776v1.summary: 本論文は、Coxeter群およびHeckeモノイドにおけるtwin準同型問題に動機付けられ、Artinモノイドの標準準同型とその合成から導かれる広範な解のクラスを提示している。これらの準同型は、最適かつ生成元において単射である場合に単射となることが期待され、これは斉次準同型やParisによって解決されたTits予想を一般化するものである。また、互いに素な標準準同型を分類し、定義域のランクが2の場合における完全な分類を予想している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26776v1.appendix: 本論文はArtinモノイドやCoxeter群の代数的構造を扱っており、指定された分野のうち「structure of large countable infinite group」に強く関連しています。また、モノイドの準同型や生成元の関係性は「combinatorics on words」の分野とも密接に関わります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26768v1.title: Emerson-Lei elevator automata の補集合化（テクニカルレポート）
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26768v1.summary: Büchi elevator automata は、強連結成分が決定性または本質的に弱い（inherently weak）という性質を持つ Büchi オートマトンの一種であり、LTL モデル検査などの実用的な応用に広く現れる。本論文では、これを受容条件がより豊富な Emerson-Lei オートマトンへと拡張した Emerson-Lei elevator automata を提案する。さらに、一般的な Emerson-Lei オートマトンに対する従来手法よりも漸近的な計算量が大幅に改善された補集合化アルゴリズムを導入する。実験により、既存ツール Spot と比較して実用的な効率性が示されており、複雑な受容条件を持つオートマトンの実用的な処理に向けた重要な一歩となっている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26768v1.appendix: 本論文は「automata theory」および「formal languages」の分野に直接関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26747v1.title: 係数をフィボナッチ数列に制限した連分数展開の次元スペクトル
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26747v1.summary: 本論文では、一般化フィボナッチ数列 F₍ₐ₁,ₐ₂₎ に制限された係数を持つ連分数展開の次元スペクトルの構造を分析している。正の整数 a₁ < a₂ から始まる数列において、a₁ ≥ 2 または a₁ = 1 かつ a₂ ≥ 3 の場合、その連分数の集合は全次元スペクトルを持つことを証明した。一方で、Falk と Nussbaum によって開発された数値解析手法を用い、標準的なフィボナッチ数列 F₍₁,₂₎ およびリュカ数 F₍₂,₁₎ に制限された場合には次元スペクトルにギャップが生じることを示した。さらに、これら後者の場合でも、次元スペクトルが常に非自明な区間を含むことを証明している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26747v1.appendix: 本論文は、記号力学系 (symbolic dynamics) や計算機によって援用された数値解析 (validated numerics) の手法に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26709v1.title: 分散型Knowing Howにおけるモデル検査問題のΔᵖ₂完全性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26709v1.summary: 分散型Knowing How（distributed knowing how）におけるモデル検査問題の計算複雑性を調査した論文です。解析の結果、この問題が複雑性クラスΔᵖ₂において完全（Δᵖ₂-complete）であることを示しています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26709v1.appendix: 本論文はモデル検査の計算複雑性を扱っており、提示された興味ある分野の中では『automata theory』や『formal languages』における形式手法の側面と関連があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26705v1.title: 深層学習のアルゴリズム的基礎：計算量理論的収束レートと普遍近似の性格付け
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26705v1.summary: 本論文は、順伝播型ニューラルネットワーク（NN）の表現力を、従来の最適基底展開という視点に加え、計算モデルとしての側面から再考している。実数値回路で計算可能な関数は、その回路の深さや幅、ゲート構造に基づいた複雑さでNNにより近似可能であり、NNの複雑さは正則性だけでなくアルゴリズム的複雑さによって支配されることを示した。また、並列化条件を満たす定義可能なNNモデルが普遍近似器であるための必要十分条件が非アフィンな非線形性を持つことであることを明らかにした。この理論により、Newton-Raphson法などの数値アルゴリズムの模倣や、グラフの最短経路計算において従来のLipschitz近似のスケールであるO(ε⁻ᶜᵏ²)を指数関数的に改善するO(log(1/ε))のパラメータ数での近似が可能であることを実証している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26705v1.appendix: 本論文で示された数値アルゴリズム（Newton-Raphson法等）の模倣は「validated numerics」に関連する内容を含んでいます。また、回路計算に基づくNNの解析手法は「automata theory」等の計算モデルに関する分野と関連性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26685v1.title: 非一様なオートマトン族の複雑さに対して、サイズとシーリングの境界はどのように影響を与えるか？
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26685v1.summary: 本論文では、状態数やスタック状態数が制限された2方向有限オートマトンおよびプッシュダウンオートマトンの族について研究している。特に入力長が有界な場合に、これらがアドバイス付きの領域計算量クラスと直接的な関係を持つことに注目し、オートマトン族の複雑さに大きな影響を与える2つの要因として「サイズ（(スタック)状態複雑度）」と「シーリング（入力長の境界）」を定義した。これらの要因が異なる設定下でオートマトン族の計算能力にどのような影響を及ぼすかを詳細に調査している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26685v1.appendix: この論文は興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」および「formal languages」に密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26684v1.title: 並列通信有限オートマトン：非忘却モデル
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26684v1.summary: 本論文では、複数の有限オートマトンが互いの状態を照会することで通信を行う並列通信有限オートマトン（PCFA）のより現実的なモデルとして、照会中に自身の状態を保持する「非忘却（non-forgetting）モデル」を導入した。このモデルの計算能力を従来の忘却型システムや多ヘッド有限オートマトンと比較した結果、多くのバリアントにおいて、オートマトン数と同数のヘッドを持つ多ヘッド有限オートマトンと同等の能力を持つことが示された。ただし、非帰還モードの決定性集中型システムは例外的に厳密な包含関係が成り立つ。本研究により、従来の忘却型モデルにおいて未解決であったいくつかの問いに回答が与えられている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26684v1.appendix: 本論文は、興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」および「formal languages」に密接に関連しています。従来のモデルにおける未解決問題に対し、非忘却モデルの性質を通じてアプローチしている点が特徴です。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26683v1.title: 半透明な入力文字を持つ有限オートマトンに関するいくつかの未解決問題について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26683v1.summary: 半透明な入力文字を持つ有限オートマトンは、非連続的な入力処理を可能にする計算モデルであり、状態に応じて特定の記号をスキップする「半透明性」を特徴とする。本論文では、先行研究で提案された「帰還型(returning)」および「非帰還型(non-returning)」の2つのモデルについて、長年未解決であった性質を解明している。具体的には、非帰還型モデルにおける連結、クリーネ閉包、反転、逆準同型の下での非閉包性を示し、帰還型モデルについても逆準同型の下で閉じていないことを証明した。さらに、非帰還型モデルの空性判定問題が決定可能であることを明らかにした。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26683v1.appendix: 本論文は、興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」および「formal languages」に深く関連する内容となっています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26682v1.title: Idefix-Free言語とその外部文脈文法における応用
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26682v1.summary: 正規言語の真の部分族である選択言語を用いた文脈文法の表現能力に関する研究。本論文では、infix-free、prefix-free、およびsuffix-free言語（これらを総称してidefix-free言語と呼ぶ）に着目し、有限言語、monoidal言語、nilpotent言語、可換言語などの他の劣正規（subregular）言語族と比較を行っている。さらに、外部文脈文法によって生成される言語族の階層構造をこれらの新しい選択言語のタイプと比較することで、既存の階層を拡張している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26682v1.appendix: 本論文は、興味ある分野のうち「formal languages」および「automata theory」に直接関連しています。特に、正規言語の様々な部分族が文脈文法の記述能力にどのような影響を与えるかを分類・比較しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26680v1.title: 2ヘッド2次元帰還有限オートマトン
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26680v1.summary: 本論文では、矩形配列（画像言語）上で動作し、2つのヘッドが互いに逆方向に移動する「2ヘッド帰還有限オートマトン」(2-HRFA)を導入した。2-HRFAが受理する言語クラスは、文脈自由行列文法(CFMG)が生成するクラスと比較不能であり、帰還プッシュダウンオートマトン(RPDA)が受理するクラスの真部分集合であることを示している。また、両ヘッドが同期して移動する制約付きの「両ヘッドステップ2ヘッド帰還有限オートマトン」(B2-HRFA)を定義し、包含関係 RFA ⊂ B2-HRFA ⊂ 2-HRFA が成り立つことを証明した。さらに、これらの言語族における閉包特性についても検討している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26680v1.appendix: 本論文は「automata theory」および「formal languages」の分野に密接に関連しており、特に2次元の画像言語を扱うオートマトンの階層構造や閉包性に関する理論的枠組みを提供しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26679v1.title: Sparse Counting-Setsを用いた効率的な正規表現マッチング
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26679v1.summary: 数値による範囲指定を伴う計数操作付き正規表現（c-regexes）において、複数のカウンタ値を一括更新するcounting-setデータ構造が提案されているが、分岐遷移時の複製コストが性能のボトルネックとなっていた。本論文では、必須のカウンタ値のみを管理することで複製のオーバーヘッドを削減するsparse counting-setアプローチを提案し、より効率的なマッチングアルゴリズムを実現した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26679v1.appendix: 本論文は興味ある分野のうち、automata theoryおよびformal languagesに関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26678v1.title: 効率的なバックトラッキング型正規表現マッチングのための選択的メモ化
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26678v1.summary: バックトラッキング型の正規表現マッチングエンジンは、強力な表現力を持つ一方で、最悪の場合に指数関数的な実行時間を要するという課題がある。メモ化は冗長な計算を排除して線形時間を保証する有力な手法だが、完全なメモ化はメモリ消費が激しく実用的ではない。本論文では、オートマトンの最小フィードバック頂点集合の計算に基づく「最小フィードバックノード（MFN）メモ化スキーム」という選択的メモ化戦略を提案する。提案手法と既存のメモ化手法との関係を明らかにするとともに、ThompsonおよびGlushkovのオートマトン構成法における挙動の解析を行っている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26678v1.appendix: 本論文は、提示された興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」および「formal languages」に密接に関連しています。オートマトンのグラフ構造解析（フィードバック頂点集合）を正規表現のマッチング最適化に応用する手法を扱っています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26677v1.title: 脱出するアリをどの程度の期間閉じ込めておけるか？
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26677v1.summary: ラングトンのアリは、長期的には複雑な振る舞いを示し、最終的に有限の連結領域から脱出することが知られているが、その定量的な性質は十分に解明されていない。本論文では、アリが領域を離れるまでに行う最大ステップ数である「脱出時間（escaping time）」を研究した。領域サイズに応じた一般的な上界を確立し、特に正方形領域では階乗の上界、高さが2および3の長方形領域では線形の上界、固定された高さの長方形領域では多項式の上界を導出した。また、対称性を利用した最適化アルゴリズムとバックトラッキングを用いたシミュレーションによって厳密な値を計算し、線形上界が漸近的に最適であることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26677v1.appendix: 本論文はセル・オートマトンを扱っており、指定された興味ある分野の中では「automata theory」や「complex dynamics」に深く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26665v1.title: 局所分岐における指数的に小さい分離現象に関連する内部問題への幾何学的アプローチ
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26665v1.summary: 本論文では、局所分岐の展開における2次元の形式的接続に関連する「内部問題」を幾何学的に扱う手法を提案している。具体的には、独立変数 x ∈ ℂ および θ ∈ ℂ/(2πℤ) を持つ非線形偏微分方程式 x² y'ₓ(1+O(x)) + y'θ + x A y = O(x²) を対象とし、その解がGevrey-1型の係数を持つフーリエ級数のxに関する1-和（1-sum）であることを示した。この手法は、zero-Hopf分岐や共鳴Hopf-Hopf分岐といった例に応用され、不変多様体をブローアップ座標を通じて相空間上で直接表現することを可能にする。技術面では、BonckaertおよびDe MaesschalckによるBorel-Laplace法を解析的なフーリエ級数へと拡張し、Borel平面上で指数成長を持つ係数を含むフーリエ級数のBanach空間において偏微分方程式を解決している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26665v1.appendix: 本論文は、解析的な微分方程式や不変多様体の研究を扱っており、複素力学系（complex dynamics）の分野と深く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26605v1.title: ランダムおよび同時力学系における乗法的エルゴード定理
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26605v1.summary: 本論文では、コンパクトな確率空間上で定義された測度保存写像の有限集合を対象とし、力学系の成長に関する2つの側面を考察しています。第一に、無限語によって決定される経路に沿った点軌道の進化を扱う設定、第二に、集合の軌道が進化し得るすべての可能な経路を考慮する集合値の設定です。これら2つのケースに対して、Oseledetsによる乗法的エルゴード定理の完全な記述を与えることを目的としています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26605v1.appendix: 本論文は興味ある分野のうち、symbolic dynamics および combinatorics on words と密接に関連しています。特に、写像の適用順序を決定する無限語の扱いは、記号力学系や語の組合せ論的な手法と親和性が高い内容となっています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26525v1.title: 計算機科学のための論理学における理論規模の自動形式化
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26525v1.summary: 既存の自動形式化研究が個別の命題に焦点を当てていたのに対し、本研究では数百もの相互依存する定義・補題・定理を整合的に翻訳する理論規模（theory-scale）の自動形式化に取り組んでいる。著者らは計算機科学の論理学に基づいたベンチマークLCS-Benchを提案し、概念グラフや反例探索を活用したエージェント的パイプラインと専門家の査読を通じて、Lean言語による膨大な宣言とコード群を構築した。定義の等価性チェッカーを含む新しい評価プロトコルを用いた実験の結果、現状の最高性能モデルでも20.1%の達成率に留まることが明らかになり、理論規模の形式化における課題と今後の方向性を提示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26525v1.appendix: 本研究は計算機科学における論理学を題材としており、形式言語 (formal languages) やオートマトン理論 (automata theory) に関連する内容を含んでいます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26503v1.title: ラベル付き有限オートマトンにおける2次過去状態不透明性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26503v1.summary: 本論文では、あるエージェントが、別のエージェントが現在および過去の観測に基づいて有限オートマトンの状態を一意に特定できたかどうかを確信できないという性質を、2次過去状態不透明性（order-2 bygone-state opacity）として定式化している。並行合成（concurrent composition）と古典的なオブザーバの手法に基づき、この性質を二重指数時間で検証する手法を導出した。この研究の意義は、有限オートマトンの推論を単一のエージェントから、順序関係のある2つのエージェントへと拡張した点にある。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26503v1.appendix: 本論文は「automata theory」に関連する研究であり、オートマトンのセキュリティやプライバシーに関する特性である不透明性の検証を扱っている。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26490v1.title: VeriFastのためのLLM生成仕様に関する経験的研究
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26490v1.summary: 静的検証ツール、特に分離論理（Separation Logic）に基づく検証器は、ヒープ操作を伴うプログラムの検証に優れているが、仕様記述に多大な労力を要する。本論文では、VeriFastを用いた303個のC関数に対し、LLMによる仕様生成の性能を包括的に評価した。8つのプロンプティング手法と10種類のLLMを検証した結果、機能の保持率は91%以上と高い一方、検証の成功率は31.4%に留まった。主なエラーの94%は、分離論理検証器に特有のドメイン知識の不足に起因している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26490v1.appendix: 本論文は形式仕様と言語を扱っており、[興味ある分野]の中では 'formal languages' と関連があります。また、論文内ではGemini 2.5 Pro（原文の記載通り）が高い成功率を示したことが報告されています。

papers.title: Residual-Guided Dictionary Learning for Spectrally Accurate Koopman Approximation
papers.summary: Koopman theory promises linear structure in nonlinear dynamics, but numerical Koopman spectra are easy to compute and hard to trust. A finite EDMD matrix always has eigenvalues; the problem is that many of them may have nothing to do with the infinite-dimensional operator. In this paper we make spectral reliability the objective of dictionary learning. We train neural-network dictionaries not merely to predict the next snapshot, but to minimize Residual Dynamic Mode Decomposition residuals: operator-level a posteriori errors that test whether computed eigenvalues and modes are genuine Koopman spectral objects. To keep the learned observables from collapsing into an unstable coordinate system, the loss also penalizes the condition number of the lifted data matrix. Thus the method couples two requirements that should not be separated: small Koopman residuals and a well-conditioned representation. The result is a learned dictionary that is expressive, numerically stable, and spectrally disciplined. Across conservative and dissipative benchmark systems, the method sharply reduces spectral pollution, improves residual pseudospectral inclusion, and lowers forecast error relative to standard fixed dictionaries. On sea-surface temperature data, it gives cleaner Koopman diagnostics and substantially better one-step forecasts from noisy observations with no governing equations. The message is simple: neural Koopman learning should be judged not by prediction alone, but by whether its spectral claims can be certified. Residuals provide the certificate; conditioning makes it computable.

papers.title: Learning Unions of Intersecting Affine Modules in One Dimension with Queries
papers.summary: We study the exact learnability of finite unions of intersecting affine modules in one dimension. An affine module is a set of the form $a+\sum_{j=1}^{s}b_j \mathbb{Z}$, where $a,b_1,\ldots,b_s\in\mathbb{N}$. We say that a set definable as a finite union of affine modules is a union of intersecting affine modules if it admits a representation in which all modules have a non-empty intersection. We show that this class is efficiently exactly learnable using equivalence and subset queries. Moreover, subset queries can be replaced with membership queries when a common element is known. Our algorithm requires at most $k\log(2|x_\ell|)+2k$ counterexamples, where $k$ is the number of affine modules in the smallest representation and $x_\ell$ is the largest counterexample. This implies polynomial-time learnability in the binary representation.

papers.title: On Dense Orbit Transversality for Endomorphisms of Abelian Varieties
papers.summary: Let $X/K$ be a smooth projective variety defined over a number field and $f:X\to X$ be a morphism defined over $K$. Assuming there exists a point in $X(K)$ whose $f$-orbit is Zariski dense in $X$ and up to replacing $K$ by a finite extension, Pasten and Silverman studied the distribution of grand $(f,K)$-orbits and proved that many sets of representatives of grand $(f,K)$-orbits on various classes of varieties are Zariski dense. In particular, they showed that if $X$ is a geometrically simple abelian variety, then all such sets of representatives are Zariski dense. We demonstrate the existence of a dense set of representatives for maps on all abelian varieties.

papers.title: The Gruenberg-Kegel graph of finite solvable groups that are character-quadratic or semi-rational
papers.summary: A finite group $G$ is said to be semi-rational if the set of generators of each cyclic subgroup of $G$ is contained in at most two $G$-conjugacy classes. This is equivalent to the following condition: for every column of the character table of $G$, the values appearing in the column are contained in a quadratic extension of the field of rational numbers (possibly a different one for each column). When the analogous condition holds for the rows, that is, when the field of values of every irreducible character is contained in a quadratic extension of the rationals, we say that the group is character-quadratic (these groups are often called quadratic rational in the literature). We obtain several results concerning the structure of the Gruenberg-Kegel graph of a finite solvable group that is either character-quadratic or semi-rational. More precisely, we first provide a complete classification of such graphs in the disconnected case. Also, we prove that if the graph has at most three vertices and the group is nontrivial, then it belongs to an explicit list of $20$ graphs (in the semi-rational case, this result is proved under the additional assumption that the order of the group is not divisible by $17$), and all of them are realizable except perhaps one. Finally, we show that if the graph has four vertices, then it must have at least four edges.

papers.title: An Explication of Optimal Equidistant Codes
papers.summary: We discuss the problem of characterizing equidistant binary codes of a given length $n$ having largest possible distance and the maximum number of codewords. Such characterizations have been studied by several authors over the years and they involve symmetric BIBDs with certain parameters. In this primarily expository paper, we investigate the history of this problem and give a unified presentation of the main results. Perhaps surprisingly, researchers on this problem were unaware of early relevant work by Marrero and Butson from 1973. Also, it turns out that published results on characterizations of equidistant binary codes have missed one of the possible subcases when $n \equiv 2 \bmod 4$.

papers.title: A structure theorem for centralizers of dilations in $QI(\mathbb{R}_{+})$
papers.summary: We study centralizers of dilations in the quasi-isometry group of the positive real line. We introduce an asymptotic invariant defined via coarsely dense sequences at infinity and establish a rigidity theorem for quasi-isometries that coarsely commute with a dilation. As an application, we identify the subgroup of the centralizer consisting of elements with non-empty asymptotic invariant and prove that it is naturally isomorphic to the multiplicative group of positive real numbers.

papers.title: Impartial Combinatorial Games and the Nuclear Escalation Ladder
papers.summary: We model Herman Kahn's escalation ladder as an impartial combinatorial game. Reindexing each rung by its distance to the nuclear threshold turns the ladder into a subtraction game, the most tractable class in combinatorial game theory, and the doctrinal fact that no side wishes to fire first selects the misere convention. We prove that single-ladder stability is governed by a congruence (Theorem 4.1) and derive a ladder-design corollary that makes the burden of first escalation a function of ladder length and escalation granularity (Corollary 4.2). For simultaneous theaters we show, under normal play, that joint stability is the Nim-sum of the theater-wise escalation distances (Theorem 5.2), a condition that is neither additive nor dominated by the most dangerous theater. We then show the Nim-sum reduction fails under misere play, introduce the misere quotient as its replacement, and prove by exhaustive backward induction that for two-step escalation the quotient is the order-six monoid with generators a, b satisfying a^2=1 and b^3=b, with loss set {a,b^2} (Theorem 6.3). To our knowledge, impartial combinatorial game theory has not previously been applied to nuclear escalation ladders; the existing game-theoretic literature on escalation is classical and payoff-based.

papers.title: Powers of matrices with all principal minors equal to 1
papers.summary:
Consider a square matrix $A$ whose all principal minors are equal to $1$. Over a field, this property is inherited by any power of $A$, but this is not the case over an arbitrary commutative ring. We show that it is the case over any regular ring, and also over the ring $\mathbb{Z} / d$ for any integer $d$, and in some other settings (quotients of Prüfer domains and principal quotients of normal domains). This generalizes Problem B5 of the 2021 Putnam contest.
  Over arbitrary commutative rings, we identify a stronger property that is always inherited by powers: We say that a matrix $A = \left(a_{i,j}\right)_{i,j\in\left[n\right]}$ is strongly $1$-principled if all its diagonal entries are $1$ and if all the cyclic products $a_{i_1, i_2} a_{i_2, i_3} \cdots a_{i_k, i_1}$ with $k>1$ vanish.
